title: Panthers Projected to Take Enormous Risk on Top-10 Draft Prospect in 2027
full_text:
While the Carolina Panthers play their first Sunday Night Football game in 10 years tomorrow night, it's never too early to look towards the spring, when the season is over and the draft boards are set.
The NFL Draft looms large for every team in the league, and teams quickly highlight their biggest roster needs. Carolina has mostly succeeded on offense throughout the first three weeks of the season.
QB Bryce Young has started the year exactly as Panthers fans wanted, taking another step forward and posting phenomenal numbers. Young leads the league in passing yards so far this season, throwing for at least 290 yards each game.
With Young playing well, Carolina doesn't need to look at QB options in this loaded class just yet. One mock draft has the Panthers selecting an elite talent, though with some concerns.
As far as pass rush goes, the past year has been brutal for Carolina. In 2025, the Panthers had the NFL's worst pass rush, finishing in the bottom three in both sacks and QB hits for the season.
After an awful pass-rush season, Carolina made a splash move, signing Jaelan Phillips to a lucrative multi-year deal. Thats where the positive news ends, though.
On the first day of training camp, Phillips' running mate and rising star, Nic Scourton, tore his ACL, ending his season before it even began. Given all that, if Carolina is picking in the top 10, then of course another premier pass rusher makes sense.
CBS Sports' Mike Renner dropped his 2027 NFL Mock Draft. In that mock, the Panthers were picking seventh overall and selected South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart.
Stewart is a monster off the edge. Over two seasons and into the beginning of 2026, he's posted 57 tackles, 37 of them solo, 11 sacks, 6 forced fumbles, and 3 passes defended.
Entering this season, there was real buzz about Stewart being the best overall player in this class, regardless of position. Now, through four weeks of the college football season, Stewart's draft stock has only tanked; here's why.
Stewart started the season injured, missing the first two games due to a lingering back injury. That's not the worst part, though. Stewart's behavior has become one of the biggest stories in all of college football.
In a blowout loss to Alabama, Stewart's awful temper dominated the headlines. Two major incidents occurred, the first was an act of violence, in which Stewart punched Alabama TE Josh Ford after the Crimson Tide scored a touchdown.
The second piece of Stewart's misbehavior was disobeying his own coaching staff. Stewart was seen refusing to come out of the game despite coaches telling him to, which is completely inexcusable and will have NFL front offices questioning his character.
After the Alabama game, Stewart received two suspensions, the first coming from both the SEC and South Carolina, for one game due to the punch. The second is from South Carolina, and that suspension is indefinite.
Shane Beamer on what will determine Dylan Stewart returning to South Carolina's program: "Me." pic.twitter.com/QXAFoUExfZ
So now theres major questions about how much Stewart will actually play this season. Both suspensions are justified; losing your cool and taking it out on your opponent and even your own coaching staff is childish behavior.
That said, if Carolina's top need is indeed a pass rusher, and Texas' Colin Simmons is already off the board, then Dylan Stewart is the clear choice. Stewart's 6'5 ", 250-pound frame, combined with his absurd speed, makes him a can't-miss talent.
There has to be personal growth throughout the rest of this season. If Stewart wants to keep his draft stock high, he should use this as a wake-up call and act accordingly from here on out.

title: Will the Panthers Beat the Lions? Here Are Our Staff Predictions for SNF
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers come into Sunday Night Football , their first primetime game this season, with an ugly injury report . Damien Lewis, Mike Jackson, and Jaycee Horn are out. Monroe Freeling, Xavier Legette , Jalen Coker, Lee Hunter, Bryce Young, and Princely Umanmielen are banged up, and some could miss Sunday's game, too.
The Detroit Lions are comparatively healthy, and they have what it takes to exploit the injuries the Panthers are facing on both sides. Aidan Hutchinson would love if Freeling was out, and Amon-Ra St. Brown is licking his chops that Horn and Jackson are.
Can the Panthers possibly stage an upset? Will they hang tough in a game they are clearly overmatched in? Here's what the Panthers on SI staff predicts.
Given the state of both defenses, the Lions' ineptitude and the Panthers' injury woes, it won't be shocking if both clubs hit the 30-point mark. Carolina will struggle to stop Jahmyr Gibbs late in the game. Bryce Young and company will move the ball, but settle for more field goals than touchdowns.
The only thing that might slow down the offenses is the weather. The Panthers' defense is ravaged by injuries, and the Lions are one of the worst possible matchups in this scenario. The Lions' defense is just bad, so while the offense is depleted, it still has Bryce Young, who should be able to carve up the secondary, rain or not. It just won't be enough to keep up with what the Lions are surely going to do to Akayleb Evans and Will Lee III.
Carolina has to start fast against what’s been a poor pass defense thus far in the Lions. This is a prime bounce-back spot for Brad Idzik’s offense despite the potential lack of receiver depth with Coker and Legette questionable. That said, Detroit's offense is even better than Carolina’s, and the Panthers' defense failed their first test against a great offense in Chicago. Lots of points in this game, but Detroit produces 1-2 more explosives, which will be the difference.
I think the Panthers keep this closer than some people expect. Bryce Young has played well enough through three games to give Carolina a chance, and Detroit's defense has shown it can give up some yards. But with the Panthers missing both starting corners and dealing with injuries all over the offense, I just don't know if they have enough to keep up with Detroit for four quarters. Give me the Lions in a close one.

title: Panthers Red Zone Report: 360 Yards Meant Nothing Without Touchdowns
full_text:
I like Ryan Fitzgerald. He's been really good for the Panthers, and I'm definitely not going to complain about a guy making all four of his field goals.
I just don't want to see him that much.
That's probably what bothered me most about the Cleveland game. Carolina finished with 360 yards of offense and outgained the Browns by more than 100 yards. Bryce Young threw for 291, Chuba Hubbard ran for 82, and, looking at those numbers, you'd probably think the Panthers scored more than 18 points.
They didn't. Carolina kept moving the ball, getting close enough to score and then settling for three points. Somehow, the Panthers still had a chance to win the game at the end.
I know I've talked about the offensive line a lot this week. I'm starting to sound like a broken record, but after watching Bryce Young get pressured on 51 percent of his dropbacks in Cleveland, it's hard not to keep coming back to it.
Then there's the fact that he threw the ball 48 times. Maybe I'm making this too simple, but if your quarterback is getting pressured that much, I'm not sure asking him to throw it nearly 50 times is helping anybody.
Cleveland deserves some credit. The Browns did some things up front that Carolina didn't handle very well, and sometimes the other team just beats you. That's football.
The problem is it doesn't get any easier this week. Aidan Hutchinson is coming to Charlotte, Damien Lewis has already been ruled out, and Monroe Freeling is questionable. Freeling did practice fully Friday, so maybe he's able to go, but this isn't exactly great timing for an offensive line that's already had some problems.
I'm not expecting Carolina to keep Hutchinson away from Young all night. Just don't let him wreck the game, and please don't put Bryce in another situation where he has to throw it 48 times.
This is the part I don't understand.
The Panthers weren't going three-and-out all afternoon. They moved the football and got themselves into scoring range. Fitzgerald made field goals from 35, 41, 53, and 37 yards, so he did his job every time Carolina sent him out there.
That's 12 of Carolina's 18 points coming from the kicker.
The Panthers didn't finally get into the end zone until there was 4:31 left, when Bryce found John Metchie III from eight yards out. It was a good drive, and it showed Carolina could finish one. I just kept wondering where that had been the rest of the afternoon.
Maybe that's why I'm not overly impressed by the 360 yards. It's nice, but what did it really get them? Carolina lost the game.
That's what has to be different against Detroit. If the Panthers put together a couple of nice drives Sunday night and both end with Fitzgerald kicking field goals, I'm probably going to start getting a little nervous.
Detroit can score. Trading touchdowns for field goals usually doesn't end well.
I'd start with Chuba Hubbard.
He had 19 carries for 82 yards against Cleveland, which comes out to a little over four yards per carry. Nothing spectacular, but I'll take it. If giving him a few more carries keeps Young from having to throw the ball nearly 50 times, that sounds pretty good to me.
I'd also try to make things a little easier on Young when the pressure starts coming. Get the ball out quicker. Use the tight ends. Give McMillan something underneath. It doesn't always have to be a big play.
Then, when Carolina gets close, somebody has to finish it. Maybe it's Young. Maybe it's Hubbard, maybe McMillan finally gets his first touchdown. I really don't care who does it.
That's really where I'm at after Cleveland. I don't need 400 yards of offense Sunday night, and I don't need Bryce to throw for 300 just so we can talk about how good the numbers looked afterward.
Because four field goals and one touchdown almost worked against Cleveland.
I don't think it's working against Detroit.

title: 2 Panthers Disappointments I Didn't See Coming in 2026
full_text:
I know we're only three games into the season. That's way too early to start deciding what this Panthers team is or isn't.
And honestly, there have been some things I've liked. Bryce Young has played pretty well, Jalen Coker has been really good, and the defense has looked a whole lot better since what happened against Chicago.
But not everything has gone the way I thought it would. If you asked me what has disappointed me the most so far, I keep coming back to these two.
I know I've talked about Monroe Freeling a lot already, but I'm not putting all of this on him. I expected Freeling to struggle some. He's 22 years old, he's playing right tackle after spending most of his time at Georgia on the left side, and he probably got thrown into this a little sooner than Carolina wanted because of what happened with Taylor Moton.
But the whole offensive line hasn't been good enough.
The Cleveland game is the one that really bothered me. Bryce was pressured on 51 percent of his dropbacks and had to throw the ball 48 times. I know some of that comes with trying to win the game late, but that's still way too much.
Freeling has struggled, and Luke Fortner hasn't exactly made me feel any better about the center position, either. Now injuries are becoming part of the equation, too. Damien Lewis missed practice again Thursday with an elbow injury, while Freeling was limited as he works his way through concussion protocol.
So how do they turn it around? I don't think there's a complicated answer. Get healthy, give Freeling some time to figure things out, and start giving Young more time.
And maybe don't put him in a situation where he has to throw it 48 times while he's getting pressured on half his dropbacks.
Yeah, I'm going back to this again.
I know Carolina has been better the last two weeks, but I still can't completely get past what happened against Chicago. The Bears ran for 291 yards. D'Andre Swift had 157 by himself, and Caleb Williams added another 65.
That was supposed to be one of the things Carolina fixed. So when the first game of the season looked a whole lot like some of the same problems we've seen before, I was worried.
But maybe I need to start letting that game go a little bit.
Bijan Robinson had 72 rushing yards against Carolina. Quinshon Judkins had 70. That's two straight weeks where the run defense looked nothing like the one we watched against Chicago.
I'm still not completely sold, though. Jahmyr Gibbs is coming to Charlotte Sunday night, and that's going to tell me a lot more. If Carolina can keep him from taking over the game, maybe it's finally time for me to stop talking about those 291 yards.
That's really where I'm at with both of these. I'm disappointed in the offensive line, and I'm still not sure I trust the run defense. But we're three games into a 17-game season, and there's plenty of time for both to change.

title: Why the Panthers Actually Can Upset the Lions on Sunday Night Football
full_text:
Simply put, the defending NFC South champions are beaten up. Earlier this week, the 1-2 Carolina Panthers put starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson on injured reserve. That’s just the start of a long list of injuries for the team as it prepares for a Sunday night visit from Dan Campbell’s 2-1 Detroit Lions.
Left guard Damien Lewis and wide receiver Xavier Legette are out. Meanwhile, wideout Jalen Coker, right tackle Monroe Freeling, and defensive linemen Lee Hunter and Cam Jackson are all listed as questionable.
Still, hope springs eternal. Tyler Sullivan of CBS Sports pointed to five possible upsets on the Week 4 slate. And he doesn’t rule out Canales’s club evening its record this season via a victory on Sunday night.
“While the Lions look like a behemoth in this head-to-head because of their high-powered offense,” explained Sullivan, “it’s their lackluster defense that puts them on upset alert. Pretty much across the board, the Detroit defense is either at or near the bottom of the league.”
That’s pretty spot on. Dan Campbell’s club entered this week’s action ranked ninth in the NFL in total yards and rushing yards per game, while only seven teams were averaging more passing yards per contest. And you can’t get much more consistent when it comes to lighting up the scoreboard as the Lions have scored exactly 31 points in each of their first three contests. Hence, only the Buffalo Bills (101) and San Francisco 49ers (98) are ahead of Campbell’s team (93) in this category.
Of course, there’s the other side of the ball. And it’s worth noting that while Detroit’s offensive unit has reached the end zone 12 times, Lions’ defenders have already surrendered 13 offensive touchdowns—four on the ground and nine through the air. In fact, the club has actually been outscored 95-93 in its first three games.
Only the Indianapolis Colts are giving up more total yards per game, and no team in league has allowed more passing yards per contest. That’s the kind of defense that gives every opponent a chance, especially one that has shown its capable of moving the ball and putting points on the board.
Jahmyr Gibbs with a Barry Sanders-esque TD pic.twitter.com/QbPYgc0RMk
“Last week,” added Sullivan, “Bryce Young and the Panthers’ offense came back down to earth a bit, totaling just 18 points in a loss to Cleveland on the road. However, because they are facing this Lions defense, I think they’ll look more like the offense that was averaging 35.5 points per game and 409.0 total yards per game over the first two weeks of the regular season.”
The Lions have quite the 1-2 punch in running back Jahmyr Gibbs (6) and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (5). That duo has combined to score 11 of the team’s 12 touchdowns this season. Add in the fact that quarterback Jared Goff has thrown eight TD passes and has not committed a turnover means that Canales’s club is likely going to have to survive a shootout. And Detroit’s generous defense certainly gives them a fighting chance.

title: Exclusive: Jonathan Stewart Talks Panthers Injuries, Oral-B, and More
full_text:
Former Carolina Panthers running back Jonathan Stewart knows what it's like to play in the NFL and is also seeing what life is like on the other side. It has given him the perspective to discuss a wide variety of topics with Panthers on SI, including dental health, the Panthers' injuries , and his own future.
The Panthers have historically been a good rushing football team. When they're good, including last year, it's been because of a great rushing attack, more often than not. This year, that hasn't been the case.
The offense has gotten away from that identity and struggled to get back to it. As a former running back and a current fan, Jonathan Stewart has a unique perspective on what's going on.
He didn't want to reduce any problem to a one-dimensional solution, and blaming one group or one player is not always fair. Still, there's a tendency to do just that, and Stewart believes if there's one thing that's certainly contributing, it's a weakened offensive line.
"They are battling through a lot of changes up front and a lot of unexpected circumstances, such as guys going down with injuries," Stewart said. "Taylor Moton being one of those guys, you realize how good he is when he's not out there (5:04) and he hasn't been out there."
The Panthers did spend the 19th overall pick on Monroe Freeling, who is playing Moton's position, but he's going through some "growing pains" as a rookie, and the whole offense, with a new play-caller, is experiencing some growing pains as well.
Even still, Stewart feels like Chuba Hubbard is getting better. "You have to commit to it no matter what, because at some point Chuba Hubbard will find an opportunity to bust one. And I think he's been really close... He's had some runs where I was like, 'Oh, there it is.'"
In football, injuries are going to happen. As wild as this last week has been for the Panthers, it's not terribly uncommon. Teams get ravaged by injuries and lose tons of players. Jonathan Stewart knows and has experienced this.
His former teammate Jordan Gross often said playing against backups is extremely hard. "You don't really know what to expect, and so I would almost kind of look at this as, our backups, you know, have an opportunity to showcase who they really are," he said.
On the defensive side of the ball, he specifically highlighted rookie safety Zakee Wheatley for stepping in and playing well for Nick Scott. Wheatley is the highest-graded rookie per PFF this season.
He also noted rookie cornerback Will Lee III, who is now the top cornerback on the roster. "During the Chicago game, he had a rookie moment. And ever since then, you wouldn't even tell if he was a rookie or not. He's been playing really well," Stewart said.
He admitted that Lee III is no Jaycee Horn. He's no Mike Jackson, either. But, he said, Lee has a chance to make a name for himself. "He's his own man," Stewart said. "There's going to be a lot of opportunities like that this weekend for guys to step in and make a statement because no one's coming to save you," he said.
And at the end of the day, nobody cares, according to Stewart. If the Panthers lose, no one will mark it with an asterisk because of all the injuries. In football, nothing matters for very long.
Stewart added, "Even if you win a Super Bowl, no one cares besides your fans, but next year they're going to want to win another one. That's the mentality you have to have."
Jonathan Stewart suffered his fair share of injuries during his NFL career, but nothing quite like what Jonathon Brooks is going through. Heading into Week 4 in 2026, Brooks has appeared in five of a possible 51 games.
"Keep the main thing, the main thing," Stewart advised Brooks. "Don't lose the fire for what God has put in you. I'm a firm believer that God doesn't give us anything that we can't handle." Brooks has certainly been given a lot.
But at the end of the day, football is just football, and there is more to life for Brooks and others who might be struggling to stay on the field. "Luckily, he gets the opportunity to come back later in the year. He has something that he has to take care of," Stewart said.
The Panthers are 1-2 and dropping like flies, but the talk of the town isn't any of that. It's how well Bryce Young has played in his fourth season. He leads the NFL in passing.
Jonathan Stewart shared a backfield with a former number one overall pick in Cam Newton. Now, he can watch former number one overall pick Bryce Young play as a fan.
"I think everyone's born into a situation that might give you an upper hand or something tougher to crawl through. I think Bryce Young had something tough to crawl through," Stewart said, highlighting the early revolving door of coaches, GMs, and teammates with the Panthers.
But ultimately, Stewart believes it's all made Young better and more confident. He believes Young is a much more confident man now than he was, and he has the capacity to lead from the experiences he's had in the NFL.
Part of it, though, is providing Young with enough support. Or, as Stewart put it, the right seasonings. "[You] see the pieces being added to the seasoning cabinet. Before it was just pepper and salt. Now it's paprika, it's Lowry's it's all the things now. It still takes a cook to be able to put it all together, right? A master chef," he said, highlighting that Young is becoming a master chef.
Health matters in football. Staying healthy, as the Panthers are learning, is no easy feat. For Jonathan Stewart, there's more to health than just avoiding injuries. Taking care of one's teeth and mouth is vital, too.
That's why he wanted to partner with Oral-B and Crest for this promotion. "Oral hygiene is a huge thing that I think people forget about," he said. "We talk about gut health, and we talk about staying healthy, and taking care of your teeth, taking care of your mouth is a huge part of that."
Stewart was raised on Oral-B and Crest, and he's raising his own family on the brands as well. "I want it to be so much to the point where it feels weird when we haven't brushed our teeth," the former running back added.
So, when the two brands reached out, Stewart was "ecstatic." He noted, "It was an automatic yes, let's figure it out. Let's figure out how to do a partnership." That partnership includes special Panthers-branded toothbrushes and other things.
It's not always easy to stay on a routine while playing in the NFL, so Stewart always treated it like he was going to stay at someone's house.
"Oral-B, Crest, you know, the feeling that you have when you're going to be on TV, or you're going to be on an interview, or you're going to be out there playing football even, and they catch you on the sideline, you want to make sure those pearly whites are shining bright," he concluded.
For now, Jonathan Stewart is starting a podcast and becoming a bigger fan than he could be when he was playing in the NFL. But in the future, the ex-NFL star said he would one day like to get into broadcasting.
For now, though, he said, "Now that I'm retired, becoming a Carolina Panther fan for real, I'm him. I'm a Carolina Panther fan through and through. An Oregon Duck fan through and through and a Caniac [Carolina Hurricanes fan] through and through."

title: Panthers Mailbag: Injuries Keep Piling Up, Bryce Young Keeps Improving & What Is This Team?
full_text:
I don't know about you, but I feel like I've watched three completely different Panthers teams through three weeks.
Week 1 had me wondering if anything had actually changed. Then they went to Atlanta and won 34-3, and suddenly I'm thinking maybe I overreacted. Then came Cleveland, where they had every opportunity to win and somehow found a way to come home 1-2.
So if you're still trying to figure this team out, join the club. Now the Lions are coming to Charlotte for Sunday Night Football, and the Panthers' injury report seems to get longer every time I look at it.
When I saw Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson were both going on injured reserve, I actually laughed. Not because it's funny, but because it's getting ridiculous at this point.
Both starting corners at the same time, right before Amon-Ra St. Brown comes to town? Of course.
And those aren't the only injuries Carolina is dealing with. Jalen Coker has been dealing with a quad injury, Damien Lewis has an elbow injury, and Monroe Freeling is working through concussion protocol. Freeling at least got back on the field Thursday in a limited role, which is something.
But losing Horn and Jackson together is the one I keep coming back to. Now Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans, and Chau Smith-Wade are going to have to take on bigger roles against one of the better offenses in football.
Maybe one of those guys steps up. Maybe Ejiro Evero has something planned that keeps St. Brown from taking over the game. I hope so, because I don't have a great answer for how you replace two starting corners at the same time.
Every team deals with injuries. I get it. But there comes a point where you look at the injury report and think, Come on, man. How many more?
I think a lot of Panthers fans are probably there right now.
I knew we were going to have this conversation eventually, and I'm still not sure I'm ready to go there.
Bryce has 939 passing yards and seven touchdowns through three games. He threw for 361 against Chicago, followed that up with three touchdowns and no interceptions against Atlanta, and then threw for another 291 in Cleveland. If you told me before the season those would be his numbers through three games, I'd take them.
But I also watched the games, and that's why I'm not ready to make some big declaration about Bryce after three weeks. The interception at the end of the Cleveland game was bad. Carolina still had a chance to win, and that's a throw he can't make, tipped or not.
I'm not going to defend the throw just because I think he's played pretty well overall. What I don't understand is why we're asking him to throw the ball 48 times while he's getting pressured on 51 percent of his dropbacks.
Maybe I'm oversimplifying it, but help the guy out. Run the football. Keep him out of third-and-long. Give him a chance to stand in the pocket without somebody in his face all afternoon.
So, has Young turned the corner? I don't know. But am I more encouraged by what I've seen from him than I was three weeks ago? Absolutely.
Can I just see the same Panthers team two weeks in a row? Seriously, I don't think I'm asking for much here.
Chicago was awful. Atlanta was about as good as you could've asked for. Cleveland was one of those games where I sat there afterward, wondering how Carolina managed to lose it.
That's three weeks and three completely different versions of the same team. Now here comes Detroit.
Would beating the Lions get my attention? Of course it would. Detroit is good, Carolina is beat up, and it's Sunday Night Football at Bank of America Stadium. If the Panthers find a way to win this one, I'm going to look at them a little differently Monday morning.
But I'm also not going to suddenly start talking about how Carolina has arrived because it won one football game. I need to see it again.
I want to see the defense continue what it's done the last two weeks. I want to see the offense actually finish drives instead of Ryan Fitzgerald jogging onto the field every time Carolina gets close. And please, can we not have Young throw the ball 48 times again?
Maybe Sunday night is when this team starts giving us some answers, because after three weeks, I'm still sitting here with a whole lot of questions.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 4: D'Andre Swift, Luther Burden, Kyle Monangai
full_text:
When the Chicago Bears do battle with the New York Jets in Week 4, Kyle Monangai, Luther Burden and D'Andre Swift are all going to be in the lineup.
Swift, who popped up on the injury report briefly this week before being removed, is coming off a Week 3 showing that was his least productive of the season after he carried the ball 20 times for 84 yards while adding two receptions for four yards.
Monangai was even less productive, as he posted just 31 yards on 10 carries while not seeing a single target in the passing game.
Meanwhile, Burden finally found the end zone for the first time last week and finished with seven catches for 61 yards and added one carry for seven yards.
Here's what we're doing with Burden, Monangai and Swift in fantasy football in Week 4.
The Jets have been pretty giving to running backs in 2026, with Gang Green ceding the 10th-most fantasy points per contest to the position, according to CBS Sports .
When digging deeper into the numbers, we see that a lot of that has to do with the Jets giving up an ample number of passing game production and total touchdowns to running backs.
The Jets are actually giving up the seventh-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL, and the 10th-fewest to running backs specifically.
With Monangai's lack of consistent involvement in the passing game, and with Swift operating ahead of him as usual, we're benching the Bears' RB2 in Week 4.
Burden had his best game of the season in Week 3, and that was with Case Keenum under center. Burden ranked as the WR13 last week, and he now ranks as WR27 overall , according to Fantasy Pros, which puts him on the flex radar entering Week 4.
It's going to be Tyson Bagent getting the start this week, and while he is viewed as better than Keenum, Bagent is also a wild card with his very limited sample size. Bagent only has four starts under his belt, and all of them came during his rookie season in 2023.
Making this situation even more troublesome, Burden is squaring off against a Jets defense that is surrendering the eighth-fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers and the third-fewest passing yards per game overall.
We're skeptical this is the right week to start Burden.
We've already noted how stingy the Jets are to running backs on the ground, but their susceptibility to giving up receiving yards and touchdowns in general makes Swift a solid starting option because he has a regular role in the passing game.
New York is tied for the 11th-most receptions and receiving scores permitted to the position, and the third-most receiving touchdowns and 10th-most rushing scores per contest.
Those numbers, along with volume, keep Swift as a viable starting option on Sunday despite a tough matchup on the ground.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 4: Colston Loveland, Rome Odunze, Kalif Raymond
full_text:
Some of the Chicago Bears' pass-catchers have not gotten off to the kind of start we thought they would.
More specifically, tight end Colston Loveland has just five catches for 34 yards, and wide receiver Rome Odunze has pulled in eight receptions for 139 yards. Neither player has scored, but both failed to cash in on golden opportunities last week.
The surprise of the season has been wide receiver Kalif Raymond, who leads the Bears with 19 catches for 214 yards, and he has found pay dirt once.
Now, a look at if we're starting any of these players in fantasy football in Week 4, when the Bears take on the New York Jets .
What a disastrous start to the season for Loveland, who was viewed as an elite tight end option going into the campaign. Through three weeks, Loveland ranks as TE47 overall.
He had his best game of the season in Week 3 with four catches for 31 yards, but that's hardly an adequate outing, as he only ranked as TE26, per Fantasy Pros .
Now, Loveland has to catch passes from yet another quarterback, with the Bears reportedly deciding to roll with Tyson Bagent over Case Keenum.
This isn't even a positive matchup, either, as the Jets are tied for the third-fewest fantasy points permitted per contest to tight ends. They're also giving up the third-fewest passing yards in general.
There just isn't enough here to trust Loveland in lineups until we see the kind of elite performance we were expecting out of him this season.
Odunze's start to the season has not been good.
Odunze hasn't tallied more than 52 yards in a game, nor has he found the end zone. He almost did in Week 3, but he had an awful drop in the end zone on the most catchable pass you will ever see.
At this point, we have to wonder if Odunze's confidence is in a bad spot. What we can say for sure is that our confidence in the former top-10 pick is definitely in a bad spot with him ranking as WR56 overall.
All of that and we haven't even mentioned the fact that the Jets are the eighth-stingiest team when it comes to allowing fantasy points to wideouts in 2026.
When factoring everything in, including the fact that Bagent is now the starter this week, we're not letting Odunze anywhere near our starting lineups in Week 4.
At the beginning of the season, If you had told us Raymond would be the Bears' leading receiver and a viable fantasy option through three games, we would not have believed you. Yet, here we are.
Because of his impressive performances, Raymond ranks as WR12 overall, which is WR2 production. Raymond now has finishes as WR15 (Week 1) and WR7 (Week 3) this season.
Under better circumstances, we would consider Raymond a starter, but we just don't feel comfortable with Bagent under center after he hasn't made a start in three years.
We also don't like the fact that the veteran faces a Jets defense that has given up the eighth-fewest fantasy points per game to the position, and the third-fewest passing yards per contest.
There's just too much to not like about this situation to start Raymond, although we wouldn't blame you if you did given Raymond's ranking in fantasy points.

title: Bears Should Monitor Rumored Steelers, Commanders Trade Candidates
full_text:
The Chicago Bears should continue to keep an eye out for help on the interior of the defensive line and at edge rusher up until the trade deadline, which falls on Nov. 10.
Chicago's edge rushers room has been fairly solid so far this year, with Dayo Odeyingbo , Montez Sweat and Austin Booker posting five sacks combined. However, we'd feel much more comfortable with the group if the Bears had another established edge rusher.
The interior of the defensive line, on the other hand, hasn't had as much success and the trade involving Gervon Dexter isn't looking too hot right now. Bears interior defenders have combined for 11 pressures, and eight of those are from Grady Jarrett alone according to Pro Football Focus .
Chicago has only gotten one sack from the group and ranks a lackluster 22nd against the run.
Two players the Bears should keep their eyes on between now and the trade deadline are Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne and Pittsburgh Steelers edge rusher Alex Highsmith.
That's because both were mentioned as trade candidates by The Athletic's Jonathan Jones after he poked around his sources for names to watch for next month.
"After shaking down sources this week, I’m keeping an eye on a number of players," Jones said, before naming the Steelers edge rusher and Commanders interior defensive lineman.
We could see both teams unloading those defenders.
Payne is on the final year of his contract and likely doesn't have a future in Washington, and if the Commanders' season goes south before the deadline, Washington could sell off some pieces and Payne would be a prime candidate.
The Steelers still have Highsmith under contract for another year, but Pittsburgh might be more inclined to trade him now to get max value, as teams won't be willing to offer as much when he could be just a one-year rental in 2027. The Steelers will have to fall out of contention before they even consider dealing Highsmith, but the first four games have shown that's a possibility for Pittsburgh.
Payne could provide some needed juice to the Bears' interior pass-rush, with the veteran posting eight pressures this year, which is nearly more than the Bears' interior defenders have combined.
Payne was a much better run defender early in his career, but he hasn't been good the last handful of years. He does, however, have a 58.7 run defense grade , which is tied for his best mark in the last six seasons. That would rank second on the Bears behind Jarrett.
Given the fact that he's a free agent in 2027, the Bears don't have to commit to Payne long term, so that's another plus and will almost certainly keep his trade price low.
Highsmith is exactly the proven pass-rusher the Bears need along the edge. The veteran has three sacks and 10 pressures thus far, and those marks would rank first and second, respectively, in Chicago.
Last season, Highsmith had 9.5 sacks in 13 games, and he had six or more in each of the four seasons prior, including a career-high 14.5 in 2022.
He is also a strong run defender, as evidenced by his 72.2 run defense grade in 2026. That checks yet another box Chicago needs.
We suspect it'll cost at least a third-round pick to acquire Highsmith. The Bears have all of their picks over the next two years, so they'd have the draft capital to get it done, however much Highsmith would cost.

title: Coby Bryant's Cryptic Post Has Bears Fans Dreaming of Best-Case Scenario
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' defense was dealt a devastating blow during training camp when it was discovered that safety Coby Bryant suffered a long-term injury.
Bryant got hurt during practice one day and after it was initially believed he had avoided a significant injury, Bryan't injury was instead confirmed to be a four-to-six month issue .
That means Bryant could potentially miss the entire season, and a December return, at least according to the initial timeline, is the best-case scenario.
However, Bryant, who is in the midst of recovering from his small fracture that required surgery, posted a cryptic tweet on X on Friday that had many Bears fans wondering if he hinted at an earlier return.
🤫 pic.twitter.com/ZnqYOWe7X4
We have no idea exactly, but some Bears fans are taking this as a sign that Bryant could get back sooner than expected, or at least at the shorter end of the timeline.
"I’VE SEEN ENOUGH. COBY BRYANT IS COMING BACK SOON," Bearsszn wrote .
"I’m totally not gonna overreact to this," Harrison Graham of Chat Sports wrote.
"That week 6 come back gonna be meaannnn," another Bears fan wrote .
Again, we have no clue what this post actually means, but we would be lying if we said it didn't pique our interest and leave us wondering if Bryant might be back early or right at four months.
Or, maybe this post has nothing to do with his recovery timeline at all, but that's the least fun option we have here.
Bryant was signed to a three-year, $40 million contract to be the starter at safety. His return at any point would provide a huge jolt to Chicago's defense, especially because of the tandem he will form with Dillon Thieneman.
The rookie first-round pick is already playing at a high level just three games into his career and he hasn't even fully developed yet , so even better play is ahead of Thieneman.
"Each and every day, each and every week, he continues to improve," Dennis Allen said, per Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com . "He's starting to get a better feel for the defense, a better feel for how the offense is trying to attack us. He's becoming the guy that we thought that he would be when we evaluated him in college.
"I think any time you have a guy that's got the speed and the range back there, they kind of become an eraser," Allen added. "They eliminate explosive plays. He's still in the early part of his development. I think there's still a lot of growth left for him."
Putting Bryant together with Thieneman could give the Bears one of the very best safety tandems in the NFL.
And, if Jaylon Johnson can get his act together, Kyler Gordon can return and get back to form and Malik Muhammad is able to keep playing the way he has, Chicago's secondary has the potential to be scary good.

title: Bears Place Braxton Jones on IR Among 3 Roster Moves Before Week 4 Game
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are going to need Ozzy Trapilo’s improbable return from injury to become just a little more miraculous. On Saturday afternoon, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reported that Braxton Jones, who had been starting at left tackle, will be placed on IR after he sustained a knee injury in their Week 3 upset win over the Philadelphia Eagles . He’ll miss at least the next four games.
In his place, Theo Benedet is slated to start in Week 4. Barring a catastrophic performance against the New York Jets, he will likely remain the Bears’ starting left tackle until either Jones or Trapilo can return to the active roster.
The loss of Jones will hurt the Bears more than some fans may realize. While he’s not exactly a household name, the former fifth-round pick from the 2022 draft has been a reliable left tackle over the years. Through three games in 2026, he had earned a 75.8 impact grade from Pro Football Network ; a 75.0 impact grade is considered to be an average score.
The Bears made two other roster moves on Saturday, as reported by Biggs. Defensive end Marcus Davenport and cornerback Nick McCloud have both been called up from the practice squad ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Jets. This is McCloud's second season with the Bears, as he appeared in 15 games in 2025 due to several key injuries in the secondary.
Davenport just signed with the Bears in August but never really practiced in training camp. Instead, he went to the practice squad but has now been added to the active roster. While the Bears are absolutely in need of more pass rush juice along the defensive line, they're not likely to get much from Davenport. He's never hit double-digit sacks in a season before, and he racked up just 1.5 in 10 games with the Lions from 2024 through 2025.
However, it's not all bad news for the Bears, or rather they're not the only team that will be at Soldier Field tomorrow with injury woes. Multiple Jets players have been ruled out for Week 4 , including standout running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mtichell. Starting guard Dylan Parham was also ruled out, which should exacerbate the Jets' problems along the offensive line.

title: How Bears Will Replace Caleb Williams, 2 Other Injured Starters in Week 4
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have three starters set to sit out the Week 4 game against the New York Jets.
Those three starters are Caleb Williams, Braxton Jones and Cam Lewis. Williams and Jones are ruled out , and Lewis is doubtful, which makes him highly unlikely to suit up.
With those three players sidelined, the Bears need replacements. Knowing that, here's how things will look on both sides of the ball against New York.
QB: Tyson Bagent RB: D'Andre Swift WRs: Luther Burden, Rome Odunze TEs: Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet LT: Theo Benedet LG: Joe Thuney C: Garrett Bradbury RG: Jonah Jackson RT: Darnell Wright
The Bears have been running multiple tight-end sets (12 and 13 personnel) for a shade over 50% of their snaps , which is why we have Kmet listed as a starter. Kalif Raymond is the third wide receiver when Chicago runs three wide receivers sets.
Head coach Ben Johnson has already stated that Benedet will take Jones' place for Week 4 . Jones suffered a knee injury last week and has been ruled out for Sunday.
Johnson had floated both Jordan McFadden and Joe Thuney as possible options, but Benedet always made the most sense. After all, he has already played snaps at left tackle this season and the Bears would have had to make two changes upfront if the team opted for Thuney instead.
Ozzy Trapilo probably would have gotten the nod if he was ready, but the 2025 second-round pick is still ramping up in his return from a torn patellar tendon.
Johnson did not want to name the team's starting quarterback for Week 4, but the decision has since leaked.
According to Dan Wiederer of The Athletic , the Bears are set to start Bagent over Case Keenum .
Bagent is the team's real No. 2 quarterback but didn't start in Week 3 because he didn't have enough time to prepare due to being in the concussion protocol.
Johnson has stated he believes that Bagent is one of the best 32 quarterbacks in the NFL, which goes to show how highly the Bears think of him.
DEs: Montez Sweat, Dayo Odeyingbo DTs: Grady Jarrett, Kentavius Street LBs: Devin Bush, T.J. Edwards CBs: Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad (slot) S: Dillon Thieneman, Xavier Woods
We're not sure if it was because Stevenson wasn't 100% or if there was simply a changing of the guard, but Muhammad played 40 of his 44 snaps on the boundary in place of Stevenson last week. Meanwhile, Lewis was the primary slot cornerback.
From there, Woods will play at safety alongside Thieneman, where the veteran was deployed last week.
Things could get even more interesting in Week 5, as Kyler Gordon looks set to return to action from the PUP list after he logged three full practices during the week.
Once Gordon is fully ramped up, he should take over in the slot, in which case the Bears should move Muhammad outside full time, leaving Stevenson out in the cold, at least for now, as Johnson remains vulnerable due to his poor start to the season.

title: Nahshon Wright’s Struggles With Jets Put His Bears Breakout in Perspective
full_text:
Former Chicago Bears cover man Nahshon Wright was one of the biggest surprises across the entire NFL last season.
He started 16 games for Chicago and led the league with 8 total takeaways, which included 5 interceptions and 3 fumble recoveries. The (then) 27-year-old made the Pro Bowl for his efforts.
The breakout campaign came one season after he spent the entire year on the Vikings practice squad. Wright started only three games over his first four years before bursting onto the scene.
5th interception of the year for Nahshon Wright! pic.twitter.com/NnOjbcA2ID
Unfortunately, Wright's affinity for takeaways was much stronger than his overall coverage chops. He was often caught out of position, and tended to be slow to react in man-to-man situations. Other teams clearly focused on that fact, rather than his ball production, via free agency,
He eventually settled for a one-year, $5.5 million prove-it deal with the Jets this offseason. That was the league saying they needed to see him do it again before anyone would commit to him long-term.
Unfortunately, Wright hasn't proven anything through the first three games. Not only has he failed to crack the starting lineup, but he also hasn't seen a defensive snap since arriving in New York. He's been limited to 18 special teams snaps thus far.
Could Wright's iconic 2025 campaign really be nothing more than a flash in the pan?
If Wright's 2025 campaign proves to be a one-off, then it's one of the best one-hit wonders in recent memory . Sure, the coverage struggles were always glaring, but you can't luck your way into eight takeaways. Even in today's passing league, that doesn't happen.
Nevertheless, Wright's career seems to be careening towards Tubthumping by Chumbawamba status (if you don't know what I'm talking about, then that proves my point). At 28, he's not getting any younger, and that fact matters a lot for a cornerback. He'll be hard-pressed to find another starting opportunity next season if he fails to catch on in New York.
Instead, giving defensive coordinator Dennis Allen and secondary coach Al Harris their flowers seems apt. They helped resurrect his career in a way that New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, one of the league's most respected defensive shot-callers, is struggling to do .
Harris, specifically, seemed to tap into Wright's potential. The cornerback credited the coach as a major reason for his success.
“Everything. I think he’s the reason why I’m standing here today.” Nahshon Wright on what Al Harris means to the Chicago Bears: pic.twitter.com/B5jalvViKb
Harris was a major factor in their decision to bring Wright to Chicago during the 2025 offseason. He was the Cowboys' defensive back coach when the team selected him in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft.
While he isn't solely responsible for Wright's 2025 breakout, it can effectively be considered another feather in his already impressive cap. He might have to make room for another one if the Bears' fourth-round selection continues on his current trajectory.
We hate to kick Wright when he's down, but the Bears are in a much better spot at the cornerback position with Malik Muhammad II. Ryan Poles and Co.'s decision to trade up for him in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft was one of their best of the offseason .
Alongside Dillon Thieneman, the rookies have played like their two best members of the secondary to begin the season. Dennis Allen has already gone so far as to say that Muhammad might be their best cover man .
Muhammad has only allowed a passer rating of 28.5 through the first three games. He's only allowed five completions (off 12 targets) for 76 yards in coverage. Harris has also taken notice of his quick start.
Al Harris on what excites him about #Bears rookie Malik Muhammad: “Everything.”🔥 pic.twitter.com/6gd3e8m7ss
It's still too early to definitively say the Bears landed a steal, but that certainly appears evident through three games. He's still only scratching the surface of how good he can become.
Their decision to let Wright walk may have been polarizing (considering how much he signed for), but it appears to have been a blessing in disguise. They probably wouldn't have prioritized the position in the draft had he stuck around.

title: Bears Catch a Big Break for Week 5 with Latest Packers Injury Update
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' defense caught a break for their Week 4 matchup against the New York Jets, with multiple Jets offensive playmakers ruled out, and it looks like the Bears' offense will get their turn in Week 5. According to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Green Bay Packers superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons is "not expected to practice next week" ahead of their Week 5 game against the Bears, and "it could be November before he's ready" to return.
Shortly after tearing his ACL last December, there was optimism that Parson's injury return timeline could only stretch to September, which would make him available at the start of the season. That was always a longshot, however, and now it appears he will miss his third straight Bears-Packers rivalry game.
You never want to see injuries to NFL players, especially not to game-wreckers like Parsons. But the toothpaste can't be put back in the tube, and the Bears' offense can breathe a little easier in Week 5 knowing that they won't have to face a motivated Micah Parsons.
There's no denying that Parsons is the kind of player who can completely change the trajectory of any given game or even an entire season. There's a reason why the Packers became Super Bowl favorites after their blockbuster trade with the Cowboys last year. However, he has only appeared in one Bears-Packers rivalry game thus far, and he was almost a complete nonfactor in that one.
During Chicago's Week 14 loss to the Packers at Lambeau Field, Parsons got plenty of pressure on Caleb Williams, but his final statline showed only one tackle, with no sacks or forced fumbles. Beating the Bears despite poor production from Parsons was surely encouraging to the Packers, but they didn't trade two first-round picks and a good defensive tackle for only marginal benefits against their division rival.
As Pelissero noted, the hope is that Parsons will be able to return in November, which means he's practically guaranteed to be available for the Packers' Christmas day showdown against the Bears at Soldier Field, barring any setbacks in his recovery. That's good news for Green Bay, but they'll still need to hold a cautious, collective breath until he can prove that he's back to his dominant self.
Parsons' first game agains the Bears as a Green Bay Packer may not have been what he envisioned, but there's no doubt that he's the kind of player who can take over any game at the drop of a hat. If he was available for Week 5, the Bears would have had to devote serious attention to him, even coming off a major injury.
But with this latest injury update, it looks like the Bears will once again dodge a bullet. The biggest question facing Chicago for their Week 5 matchup with the Packers remains whether Caleb Williams will return from his injury in time to play.

title: Case Keenum Endorses 'Baller' Tyson Bagent as Bears Stay Mum on QB1 vs. Jets
full_text:
There is healthy competition in the Bears' quarterback room as Caleb Williams recovers from his hamstring injury .
So healthy, in fact, that Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent are happy for the other when called upon by Ben Johnson and Co.
Keenum specifically endorsed Bagent as not only a "baller," but someone who can potentially do the job even better than him if given the chance.
Keenum is coming off a three-all-purpose-touchdown season debut against the Eagles on Monday Night Football this past week, completing 24-of-34 pass attempts for 247 passing yards. That is a bold claim from the 38-year-old.
"You've got to be ready to go, and that's how I prepare every week. It doesn't matter what reps you're getting or not, you've got to be ready to go, so I'll be ready to go this week," Keenum said this week .
"It's not like we've been sitting on the couch eating potato chips. We've been working our tails off. Part of this job is preparing, and when preparation meets the opportunity, that's what it looks like. And if his name is called, I expect the same, if not better. He's a baller."
It'd be a major upset if Bagent didn't get the start against New York this coming Sunday afternoon at Soldier Field.
Keenum claiming that Bagent could potentially be better if given the call sounds like a grizzled vet who knows someone 12 years his junior is probably getting the call.
Bagent got limited reps against the Vikings in a 9-3 loss during Week 2, but he completed five-of-nine pass attempts. During the preseason, he completed 29-of-39 passes for 377 passing yards, three touchdown tosses, and one interception.
After being impressed with Keenum's performance, Bagent, who admitted he took notes on it, will get his chance to show what he can do under center on Sunday.
As valuable as those notes were, Bagent will have to beat the Jets in a different way than Keenum beat the Birds.
Keenum got the ball out quickly and let his playmakers work. Philadelphia's pass rush, which is fifth-to-last in the league in sack rate, had just 10 pressures the whole game. Keenum was able to pick apart the Eagles from the pocket with minimal stress.
Bagent has a big arm, but New York's secondary is No. 4 in air-yardage allowed through the first three weeks. Given the lack of pressure this past week, with rookie David Bailey having the only pressures for the Jets against the Lions, perhaps a heavy dose of play-action is in the cards for Chicago's offense. Bagent's speed will enable a horizontal attack.
If Johnson makes the obvious QB1 choice for Week 4, he has to switch up his blueprint.
Few are more willing and able to do that week to week than the Bears' fearless leader.

title: Bears Rumor Confirms Chicago's Week 4 QB Decision Between Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have reportedly made their decision about who will start between quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum in Week 4 against the New York Jets.
When asked about who would start on Friday after Caleb Williams was officially ruled out again due to his hamstring injury, head coach Ben Johnson decided to keep it close to the vest .
However, the Bears head coach wasn't able to keep it secret for long. According to The Athletic's Dan Wiederer , the Bears are going to start Bagent in Week 4 versus the Jets.
"The Chicago Bears are switching lanes at quarterback again, with Tyson Bagent now in line to start Sunday’s home game against the New York Jets, according to multiple sources who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly about the decision," Wiederer wrote.
Of course, the Bears gave the ball to Case Keenum last week after Bagent, who is officially the team's No. 2 quarterback, wasn't ready to start after not being involved in the game plan much.
That was because Bagent spent most of the week recovering from a concussion that prevented him from being in the building early in the week. Bagent was active on gameday, though, and served as Keenum's backup.
Keenum was sensational against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3, completing 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns while also adding a rushing score.
Because of that performance, many believed the Bears would stick with the hot hand, but clearly that is not the case and the Bears will instead follow their depth chart.
Johnson hinted after Monday's game that the team would turn to Bagent because, well, he's the No. 2 quarterback for a reason .
"We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said . "But I said it last week and I'll say it again: There was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."
The Bears have a ton of faith in Bagent , with Johnson noting back in February that he believes Bagent might be one of the best 32 quarterbacks in the league, which means he views him as a starting-caliber player.
"I do think there's a merit to habing a strong No. 2 quarterback,  which he certainly fits that bill. I'm of the mind the mindset he's probably one of the best 32 (QBs) in the NFL. His preseason tape over the past few years has probably confirmed that in my opinion. But if I took myself out of the equation, I want what's best for him. If he would like an opportunity to start I certainly hope he can get that somewhere," Johnson said.
One plus for starting Bagent is the fact that he will be able to showcase what he can do as a starter, which could help Chicago flip him for a solid return down the road.
But, first things first, Bagent has to get the job done against New York on Sunday, and for as long as Williams remains sidelined, which could be a few more weeks.

title: 3 Bengals Players Who Must Step Up to Beat the Jaguars
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off an embarrassing loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cincinnati realistically should have rolled over the Steelers, but the Steelers dragged them into a dog fight and the Bengals came out on the losing end.
This week, Cincinnati matches up with the Jacksonville Jaguars, and they desperately need to bounce back in a big way.
Which players need to step up in Week 3 to get the Bengals back on track?
Rookie defensive end Cashius Howell has made an impact by generating pressure in his limited time on the field, but he hasn't made any splash plays to this point. The Bengals need him to begin converting on his pass rush wins, preferably with a big-time sack against Trevor Lawrence.
Howell has the burst to beat the Jaguars' offensive tackles, but he needs to prove that on Sunday. The Bengals have seen some sort of production from the other key pieces on their defensive front. Sunday is the perfect time for Howell to make a name for himself.
The Bengals don't have a solidified No. 3 wide receiver right now. They have one of the best wide receiver duos in the league, with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins leading the offense, but they need more. That's where tight end Mike Gesicki comes into play. Gesicki was spectacular in Week 1. He was solid last week. But he needs to be better in Week 4 to make up for the Bengals' lack of depth at wide receiver.
Speaking of the Bengals' lack of depth at wide receiver, they need to see more production out of running back Chase Brown. Brown has been the sole running back to see important touches this year, and he's been decent. The Bengals need him more involved in the passing game if they want to sustain their success. Brown is typically quite the big receiving threat out of the backfield, but he hasn't flashed that this season. Cincinnati is at its best when Brown is firing on all cylinders.
The Bengals are hoping to start 3-1 for the first time since the 2021 season when they beat Jacksonville in Week 4 to improve to 3-1 on the season. That year ended with a run to Super Bowl LVI.

title: Bengals Announce Multiple Roster Moves Ahead of Jaguars Matchup
full_text:
Cincinnati announced a few roster changes on Saturday in anticipation of Sunday's massive battle against Jacksonville for jockeying in the AFC playoff race.
"The Bengals today elevated CB Bralyn Lux and S Russ Yeast from the practice squad to the active roster for tomorrow's game against Jacksonville," the team site read. "Lux and Yeast both are classified as standard elevations. As practice squad players being elevated to the active roster for the game, they automatically will revert to the practice squad on Monday."
Both are likely insurance for the team's secondary injury problems.
The Bengals are going through the team's first big wave of injuries this season over the past few days, but the stars are healthy and hungry to bounce back from a self-inflicted loss against Pittsburgh last week.
Joe Burrow commented on the big story this week surrounding his clutch ability. It could get tested again on Sunday against fellow strong passer Trevor Lawrence.
Cincinnati is the only AFC team Lawrence has never beaten.
"I feel like I'm pretty good in those moments. I'm really confident in myself in those moments, and typically, we're going to try to get it done," Burrow said. "There's no place I'd rather be. I want it in my hands when you put the game on the line. I trust myself in those spots. I trust our guys in those spots. We feel confident that we're going to get it done."
The Bengals have found the right formula for beating Jacksonville in recent years, but this may be the best all-around Jags outfit yet.
"Well, teams haven't scored many points against them," Burrow noted. "Through these first couple of games, two of the teams got down a lot early, and that changes how the game is played. That changes a lot of things about it. We have got to score points, and we got to score points early. We know what kind of offense they have, and we got to be good in the red zone, like you said, and we got to be good on third down.
"We got to be really good situationally. It's just a kind of example ... Usually teams against us like to mix it up. Sometimes they'll double. Sometimes they'll blitz and play zone. Sometimes they'll blitz and play man. Sometimes they'll play man and double one of the guys. That's typically how teams like to play us. They like to mix it up, and so we've got to be ready for all those different things."
Cincinnati kicks off against Jacksonville on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Former Bengals Star Hints at NFL Comeback: 'I'm Back'
full_text:
Former Bengals and Texans running back Joe Mixon hasn't played in the NFL since 2024. That may change in the near future.
Mixon posted a hype video on X on Saturday teasing a possible return. The video included commentary on his status, which included a foot injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025 season.
At the end of the video, Mixon made his return clear "Let's Go! I'm back, baby!" he yelled.
Mixon missed the entire 2025 season with a foot injury. Texans general manager Nick Caserio called it a "freak" injury, but didn't offer many details.
Houston released Mixon in March after trading for David Montgomery. The Bengals traded Mixon to the Texans ahead of the 2024 season.
Mixon ran for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns in 2024 en route to a Pro Bowl. He also had 36 catches for 309 yards and another score.
Mixon spent seven seasons with the Bengals from 2017-2023. He was selected in the second round (48th overall) in the 2017 NFL Draft. He ran for 6,412 yards and 49 touchdowns in 97 regular season games. They traded him to Houston after the 2023 season.
"I appreciate my time there. I had a hell of a seven years," Mixon told Josina Anderson nearly two years ago. "When it came down to it, it was an unfortunate situation where things changed a little bit and obviously they had them fake a** beat writers, reporters. I don't care, I'm not there any more... When it come down to it, my teammates know what it is."
By the end of his tenure with the Bengals, Mixon was unhappy with his role on offense. The coaching staff had no plans of giving him 25 or more carries per game, despite Mixon voicing his displeasure behind the scenes. He opened up about his frustrations a bit with Anderson after settling in with the Texans.
"When it come down to it I'm going to do what the coach wants me to do, but at the same time I'm going to play football. That's just what it is. You're not gonna turn me into a robot," Mixon said. "You're not gonna turn me into a person that... That's not what I do. One thing that I can appreciate here [in Houston] is they utilize my skillset. I've always been a threat in the passing game and one thing about here, they give me my screens. They give me my choices, they give me flat routes that I can take. They give me all types of combinations. They utilize me."
It's unclear if Mixon will get another shot, but it's reasonable to think a team would at least bring him in for a workout. That's assuming that the video below is his way of telling NFL teams and fans that he's 100% healthy and ready to return. Watch the video:

title: Former NFL Star Reacts to Ja’Marr Chase’s Controversial Travis Hunter Response
full_text:
It has been a long week for a Cincinnati Bengals team that is ready to move on from their crushing loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. Waiting for the Bengals on Sunday is the Jacksonville Jaguars.
The Jaguars are also off to a 2-1 start on the young season. Winning this game could be massive for either team once the playoff positioning begins to take shape.
The Jaguars have a lot of young talent, which includes former Heisman Trophy winner cornerback Travis Hunter. Earlier this week, Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase was asked about his thoughts on Hunter's play in his young NFL career. Chase's response was simple : nothing.
Chase's reaction brought out opinions from everyone. But the best response may have been from former NFL wide receiver DeSean Jackson.
Jackson was a guest on 'Up &Adams' and Kay Adams asked the former receiver his opinion on Chase's response to how Hunter has changed from his first season to his second.
"You’re talking to the best receiver in the NFL and you’re talking to me about somebody that has done what so far," Jackson said . "What has (Hunter) done so far to be talked about?"
Jackson gave high praise to Chase, calling him the best wide receiver in the game when talking about the situation. For Hunter, the assignment of defending Chase on Sunday may be the hardest matchup he has faced in his young career.
Hunter entered the league open to playing both sides of the ball. This season, the Jaguars have made it clear that Hunter will be on the defensive side of the ball.
In the Jaguars' impressive win over the New England Patriots last week, Hunter grabbed the first interception of his career. But how will he fare against one of the best offenses in the league?
Chase may be entering Sunday's game with only 185 receiving yards, but that just means he's due for his first three-digit receiving yard game. He does have three touchdowns in the past two games and is on pace to tie his career-high (17 touchdowns).
The time for talking is over. It's time for the Bengals to separate themselves from other AFC contenders. That is assuming that they'll be contenders this season.

title: Dax Hill Faces Most Pressure Against Jaguars Following Position Change
full_text:
Dax Hill is set to reprise his role at slot corner after injuries to Jalen Davis and Ja'Sir Taylor forced him back inside from his boundary spot last week. He also faces pressure to perform right away, as the Jaguars have a pair of receivers who can perform effectively both inside and outside in Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers.
Washington in particular plays most often in the slot and done so at a high level. When lined up in the slot, he has seven catches for 108 yards and caught both of his touchdowns on the season from that spot. He has a total of 15 catches on the season for 221 yards, and two touchdowns.
Meyers is likely to lineup outside more often against D.J. Turner on Sunday, however he can do damage from the slot receiver spot if necessary. Meyers first score of the season came on a 32-yard catch in the Jaguars season-opener where he lined up inside.
Lawrence is off to the best start of his career this season. Despite Pro Football Focus ranking his offensive line 27th, Lawrence has averaged 7.6 yards per play with seven touchdowns to two interceptions on the season.
Much of his success has come from attacking the middle of the field where he has an 18.3 EPA across 28 attempts ranking behind only Brock Purdy.
Hill is going to have his work cut out for him on Sunday as he should primarily across Washington who has emerged as Lawrence's favorite target. He is not happy about changing positions once more, however, Hill has affirmed that he is ready and that this is an opportunity to grow further outside of playing only one position.
“I’m gonna be ready regardless of wherever I’ll be at, inside or outside,” Hill said on Wednesday. “That’s something I know I’ll be prepared for. If that’s what it’s going to be for the rest of my career, I feel like it’s another opportunity for me to grow and not limit my mindset to where I’m only playing one position.”
The Bengals face the Jaguars on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Paycor Stadium, and the game for the Bengals could come down to Hill performing well from the slot.

title: Jaguars Have Talent, But the Bengals Can Exploit These Holes
full_text:
In their toughest game of the season so far, the Cincinnati Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday for a big cat battle.
I usually go deep into data points and weaknesses of the upcoming opponent and this week will be no different, but before we start, I would be foolish to not recognize now well this Jags team has been playing for the last year.
Now, here's how the Bengals can dismantle them.
First, let's look at the quarterback matchup. Trevor Lawrence has never had success in topping Joe Burrow, but the Bengals have also pulled out two victories with Jake Browning at quarterback.
From an evaluation perspective, Lawrence is dealing right now. From a data perspective, you can get to him and force some throws.
I, once again, will be asking Al Golden to send the blitz against the opponent.
Trevor Lawrence currently has a 57.5 passer rating when facing the blitz and that ranks 30th in the league. His 5.1 yards per attempt when facing extra rushers ranks Lawrence 28th. The Jags have struggled to pick up the blitz as 53% of them have resulted in pressures. That's the 6th worst rate in the NFL.
Lawrence seems to be taking care of the ball better, but when he's blitzed, he's throwing into tight windows 22% of the time and that's the 6th highest rate for QBs. PFF has Lawrence with 5 “Turnover Worthy Plays” already and that 5.3% rate is the 6th highest in the league.
He's going to give the Bengals defense a couple chances and those opportunities usually happen when he's pressured.
Lawrence has completed just 9-of-27 pressured dropbacks this season with four throwaways, four sacks and a 47.6 PFF grade.
So, how's the Jaguars offensive line?
They're currently 30th in ESPN’s Pass Block Win Rate and 27th in PFF’s Pass Block Efficiency.
They have a rookie left guard in Emmanuel Pregnon. He's definitely had some very impressive flashes so far, but Pregnon ranks 46th out of 59 guards in PFF’s True Pass Set blocking grade (35.3).
Veteran center Robert Hainsey isn't much better with a 40.2 pass blocking grade in PFF’s True Pass Sets. That's good for 26th amongst centers.
Have you seen that the Jacksonville Jaguars have NEVER won a game when the Over/Under is above 49 points? They're 0-29 in their existence and will have another qualifying game this weekend.
But, I doubt it even gets to 50 combined points. The Jaguars are the slowest pace offense in the entire NFL. They take the most time per snap at 33.1 seconds per play.
The Bengals are 26th at 31.1 seconds per play.
You're going to have to score when you get your chances because possessions and snaps will be limited.
So where can the Bengals attack the Jacksonville defense? In the middle of the field.
The Bengals have the 5th highest rate of throwing into the middle of the field at 26.2% of their attempts. The Jaguars are currently 32nd in EPA allowed (+1.03) over the middle.
The Jaguars don't get tested over the middle often as they like to play a single high safety at the 12th highest rate (39.2%) for defenses.
Where they get tested is on deep balls with that safety in the middle of the field. 16.9% of throws against this Jags defense have gone deep and that's the 3rd highest rate in the league.
Good thing for us is that the Bengals have the highest EPA per play on deep passes (+2.59) this season.
That's largely why the Jaguars defense has allowed an explosive play on 11% of their defensive snaps this season. That's the 6th highest rate for any defense.
The Bengals are hitting explosives on offense at the 9th best rate of 10.3% of the time.
A big part of giving up explosives is because of the Jaguars blitzing and not getting to the QB.
They have generated pressure on just 37.9% of their blitzes this season and that's the 8th lowest rate in the league.
If you're not affecting the quarterback, you're just leaving less defenders in coverage.
The Jaguars are supposed to have a great pass rush. That defensive end duo deserves respect, but they're not winning right now as a unit as they rank 27th in ESPN’s Pass Rush Win Rate.
Both Travon Walker (22nd) and Josh Hines-Allen (23rd) rank in the bottom half of the top 40 pass rushers in PFF’s Pass Rush Win Rate.
On the inside, Arik Armstead and his 4.6% pass rush win rate might finally be aging. He ranks 35th of 38 pass rushing defensive tackles.
His running mate Rule Orhorhoro has an even lower 2.6% pass rush win rate. That ranks 77th of 82 interior defensive linemen.
They rely on stunts to generate pressure, so the Bengals offensive line will need to be ready for that.
If the Bengals give Burrow time, I think they'll attack these outside cornerbacks.
The boundary trio of Travis Hunter, Jarrian Jones and Montaric Brown have been targeted 38 times this season and have allowed 25 catches (66%) for 439 yards. While they've only allowed one touchdown so far, they've been penalized 4 times.
And the Jaguars have their own version of Geno Stone back there with veteran Eric Murray.
Murray has already missed 4 tackles and his 40% missed tackle rate and his 27.5 tackling grade from PFF is, by far, the worst of any starting safety in the league.
They have a solid rotation in the secondary and you don't normally see that, but the Jags will go with a light box and trust their speed on the back half.
Their 49.1% “light box” rate is 8th highest rate in the league and the Bengals are 4th best in EPA per play (+0.41) when facing light boxes.
Other than that, the Jags truly are really good and this week's preparation took me the longest time of any of the Bengals opponents so far.
Keep the game close and make the Jags fight for everything.
At the end of the day and at the end of the game, give me Burrow.

title: Zac Taylor Drops Jaguars Game Statuses For Injured Bengals Entering Week 4 Battle
full_text:
The Bengals are entering the weekend with a few big names trying to get healthy enough to play against the Jaguars on Sunday.
Head coach Zac Taylor spoke to the media after Friday's practice and gave the latest game statuses for names like Dalton Risner, Bryan Cook, Kyle Dugger, DJ Turner, Jordan Battle, and more.
Cincinnati already ruled out wide receiver Colbie Young earlier in the week, and Kyle Dugger is joining him on the sideline as officially out for the Jacksonville contest.
Risner and Cook are entering the weekend with questionable status, getting a "we'll see" from Taylor. It's been a whirlwind week for the Bengals as they try to weather cluster injuries in the secondary and wide receiver spots.
Taylor noted Battle and Turner are "good to go," while he didn't have an update on B.J. Hill. He could be questionable with Risner and Cook.
Zac says we’ll see on Cook, Risner. Battle, Turner good to go Dugger out
Looks like B.J. Hill will be upgraded to at least limited. He’s going through position drills.
All ahead of a tough matchup against a fellow AFC contender in the Jaguars.
"Yeah, they're deep. They're deep," Joe Burrow said about Jacksonville this week. "Their two edge rushers are really good ... All those guys can play really good football. Get pressure on quarterbacks to stop the run. Play with high motors. Care about it. And then the rest of their defense plays their roles really well. Understands what they're trying to do with their coverages, and I think they're really good in man coverage. I think they trust their guys on the outside, as do we. So, we'll see what their plan is early, and we'll have to be ready to adapt to whatever they're showing."
Zac Taylor knows it won't be an easy task as well.
"Yeah, it is, and we pride ourselves on being problem solvers," Taylor said about the ease of adding Mitch Tinsley back to the offense. "And Colbie was a huge part of that plan and first played the game. A lot of it had to be changed up, and so it's a challenge that's not unique to us. But we have guys that we really believe in. That's the good news. Is we're not just playing with guys that we don't think we can find a role for. They're there because they have to be everybody in that receiver room, tight end room. We feel like guys are in the opportunity. We have a lot of confidence in what they can do for us."
Cincinnati kicks off the game at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.
