title: 'I Don't Mess With Little Dudes' - Ja'Marr Chase Recalls First Time He Talked Trash to Dexter Lawrence
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase had Dexter Lawrence and Tee Higgins join him for the latest edition of his podcast, Chasing No 1, this week, and they dove into a funny trash-talk interaction Chase had with Lawrence at the beginning of training camp.
The 6-5, 350-pound Lawrence wasn't hearing it from a player much smaller than him in Chase. All the Bengals teammates looked like they had fun chopping it up.
"I know my first time when I meet a lot of people they be telling me they don't understand what I'm saying, cause I slur my words, so I be having to slow down a lot. But for him, that wasn't the case. He was just a cool dude from the jump. You know what I'm saying? He came in right away," Chase said. "I think the first time I tried to talk a little smack to him at practice, he was like, 'I don't mess with little dudes.' I just stopped messing with him. I just walked away."
Lawrence has a pretty quiet demeanor in front of cameras, but he can talk trash with the best of them in between those white lines.
Trash talk, celebrations, it's all part of the fun of NFL games, and Chase (along with Higgins) broke out a new celebration last weekend that the NFL league office is clearly much more pleased with than the people's elbow.
Neither Bengals player got fined for it after using the new motion this week.
"I can't really control what they do and how they handle it," Chase said to round out his comments on the fine he got last week. "I'm just speaking up for myself on how certain situations play out at the end of the day. When I was a kid growing up, you know what I'm saying? That's all they did when they got to the end zone. You know what I'm saying? So one of the big reasons, a lot of kids back in the day about my time are trying to get the end zone. We trying to make a celebration to do some fire stuff. They say when you get to the end zone, it's a party. You have fun in the end zone. That's what it's always been."

title: Bengals Coaches Have to Get Shemar Stewart on the Field More
full_text:
After a loss where the entire defensive line outside of Dexter Lawrence failed to generate anything positive, Zac Taylor has to get Shemar Stewart more playing time this week.
Stewart sat on the bench for the entirety of the Bengals loss to the Steelers, something that is even more egregious following Taylor's reasoning for doing so. Taylor indicated after the game that Stewart did not play any snaps because of the defensive game plan, and because he still has not practiced enough.
"There's going to be moments we get Shemar more involved, yesterday just didn't work out that way," Taylor said on Monday. "He's still nine practices in. Really started practicing three weeks ago."
Outside of Stewart's Texas A&M teammate Cashius Howell, no one has emerged as a potential difference maker in this edge rusher room. Boye Mafe had a solid start to the season, however he failed to make a meaningful impact against the run or pass against Pittsburgh. The defense as a whole managed 18 pressures this week compared to 41 in week two against the Texans.
Myles Murphy's performance in week 3 along with the interior of the defensive line is where the decision to bench Stewart feels the most questionable though. Mike McCarthy and the Steelers run game targeted Murphy often as he failed to set the edge consistently throughout the day and was largely a non-factor as a pass rusher.
At this point in time, it feels as though Murphy's ceiling is what we saw last season when he had 5.5 sacks. After declining his fifth year option this offseason and seeing how he has responded, it is in the franchises best interest to see if Stewart can develop with more reps over him.
Stewart has already eclipsed Murphy's sack production so far on the season with a half sack more on just five snaps through three weeks. He could evolve into a difference maker if given the chance as he has shown to be a capable force against the run, and create chaos for quarterbacks with his raw power and athleticism.
If the coaching staff continues to keep Stewart on the bench following their loss in Pittsburgh, it is likely a reflection of their faith in him as a contributor. He showed on his five Week 2 snaps that he is capable of playing at a fast enough speed for the game following his injury this summer.
Stewart's usage against Jacksonville is a key storyline this week as the Bengals attempt to get to a 3-1 start in the first month of the season.

title: Ja'Marr Chase Reveals How Joe Burrow Responds To Losses When The Cameras Aren't Around
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals are in full Jaguars preparation mode as Cincinnati tries to respond from its Week 3 loss against Pittsburgh. Everyone takes losing differently, and Chase touched on how he and Joe Burrow approach the days after losses.
The Bengals' best player dove into the topic with the local media on Thursday.
"Pretty much the same when he comes back in (to the building the following week). I think the biggest difference is after the game," Chase said about Burrow at the podium.
Both of the team leaders keep a good head on their shoulders, not getting too high or low after losses. They have a big task at hand this week against a Jaguars team in the driver's seat of the AFC South and eager to make real playoff noise for the first time in Trevor Lawrence's career.
"They've been having the same players since last year too. Those guys are just getting years under their belt, so they probably learned a little more," Chase said about the Jacksonville secondary before touching on how the new-look receiver depth is growing this week. "I can't really say on that because I'm not in that position. But from the looks of it, I would say those guys are handling it really well, especially Colbie (Young) making adjustments. He came in right away and knew what he was doing. So same with Dohnte (Meyers). Dohnte has been coming in off the rip and been picking up other people's reps like we practice it, so that's a good sign. And then we added Mitch (Tinsley) back into the collection because he's already been here, already knows a little bit of offense, so it's a perfect fit."
The two-time All-Pro actually just hit a milestone in his career this past weekend, a silver lining to take away from the frustrating loss.
Chase went past 7,000 career yards in the game. He is just 79 yards away from passing Isaac Curtis for third-most yards in team history, and will surely break Chad Johnson's mark (10,783 yards) in the next few years.
"I actually found out while I was shooting my podcast, and that was the first time that I knew about it. But I appreciate that, so hopefully I get more," Chase said.
Another chance to boost that tally is just a few days away.

title: 3 Keys To the Browns Finding A Fourth-Straight Win Next Sunday Against the Jets
full_text:
After defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday Night Football, the Cleveland Browns will come into week five off of what many people call a "mini bye week".
With the extra time between matchups, here are three things the Browns need to prepare if they want to find their fourth win of the season in just five games.
In the rivalry game against Pittsburgh, the Browns lost DT Mason Graham to an injury early in the game.
According to reports, Graham sprained his MCL and ankle which will sideline him for the near future.
With the teams sack leader out, the Browns must find a guy or two who will step up and fill the role.
Against Pittsburgh, the Browns were still able to apply pressure to Aaron Rodgers. If they want to get the win against the Jets, applying similar pressure to Geno Smith will be key to getting the victory.
If Cleveland is able to generate a strong pass rush and make Smith uncomfortable, expect to see some major defensive highlights from the unit.
Deshaun Watson over his last 3 games: 64-of-93 650 passing yards 5 TD, 1 INT 3-0 record The Browns now sit atop the AFC North. pic.twitter.com/dDqFhqMGi3
So far this season, Deshaun Watson has had some very high highs and some very low lows.
If the Cleveland quarterback can get to a point where he can figure out plays or formations that he is most comfortable in, the Browns can then rely on Watson to fully operate the offense at a healthy pace.
In the week four win, the Browns scored 21 points in the second quarter after being shut out in the first. After that, the Browns would only kick two field goals for the rest of the game.
At the moment, Geno Smith has been incredibly consistant with the Jets and completes about 75% of his passes.
If the Browns want to battle with a tough New York team, Deshaun Watson will have to find a way to gain yards and move the chains every drive.
After playing their fourth game of the season, the Browns have racked up a total of 43 penalties for a grand total of 297 penalty yards.
On average, thats over 10 penalties for 74 penalty yards per game.
If the Browns seriously want to do some winning and even possibly contending for the division, the penalties must stop soon.
Countless times this season already the Browns have gotten themselves in trouble by careless self inflicted wounds.
The Jets will most likely leave little room for error. If they want a chance to win, Todd Monken is going to have to do a better job at tightening up his guys before next Sunday's game.

title: Why the Browns Need to Cut Ties With This Quarterback Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are 3-1 and winning, but success has only made their quarterback dilemma more complicated.
Deshaun Watson has led the team on three straight game-winning drives and Shedeur Sanders has served as his backup. The Browns were thought to use the season to build for the future, but the future is now and the team is ready to win.
Dillon Gabriel is eligible to come off the injured reserve list and the front office has to make a decision in the quarterback room. Gabriel last played in the preseason against the New England Patriots, and threw for 186 yards with three touchdowns.
Although it was against backups and players that did not make a roster, he did look like the best quarterback in the preseason games. After the game, Gabriel was surprisingly placed on the injured reserve , making him ineligible for the team’s first four regular-season games.
It was believed that should Watson have lost the first two games, then he would have been benched for Sanders. He has earned the starting quarterback role and will keep playing as long as they are winning.
Sanders has had four weeks learning how to get through preparation under Todd Monken.
Sanders could be a trade candidate, but the NFL has shown that there has been little interest in the high-profile backup.
The New York Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy rather than checking in on Sanders. The rest of the other teams passed on him for four rounds in last year’s draft.
Gabriel should be the odd man out. It would be unwise to use three roster spots on quarterbacks, especially because Gabriel does not bring a high chance of becoming a star in the league.
The Browns have also used talented rookie Taylen Green as their emergency quarterback and his ability has too much upside to part ways in his rookie year.
They cannot afford to keep four quarterbacks on the roster going forward as it would take a roster spot away from another position on the team.
Although the Browns thought they bought enough time to evaluate and allow the play on the field to dictate the quarterback situation, the surprise start to the season changed everything. The Browns are winning, and that is all that matters.
When Gabriel comes off the injured reserve list, cutting him is the move to keep the momentum rolling.
And if not, Cleveland better be prepared to make some other sort of move to justify the roster spot.

title: Harold Fannin Jr. Reveals the Work Behind the Browns’ Late-Game Execution
full_text:
Harold Fannin Jr. described the Browns’ 27–24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers as a statement for a team that had to overcome obstacles and execute in a tense finish .
Cleveland’s tight end had three catches for 27 yards and a touchdown, and his postgame comments pointed to the preparation behind the offense’s work.
“I mean, obviously, feeling good. Beat all the obstacles. We’re juiced up, we’re pumped. I don’t know, just excited, proud of the guys, played their tails off. It was good to see all our hard work come out,” Fannin said.
The second-year tight end was asked what was working suddenly between him and quarterback Deshaun Watson.
“You know, it’s simple: practice. Talking through things…Deshaun (Watson), got me the ball; I just went out there and caught it.”
The Browns had trouble getting the offense going at times , and Fannin said the team needed to be more efficient and stay on schedule.
“Just got a little bit off schedule. We just gotta, as you said, first downs, be more efficient.”
That efficiency mattered late, when Cleveland’s offense took the field for its final drive. Fannin said the players did not need an extended conversation before heading out. They had prepared for these types of situations during training camp.
“I mean, not much for there to be said. We knew what time it was. You know, obviously throughout camp, we did situational. We already knew what the moment was; we just gotta go out there and do it.”
Fannin also celebrated kicker Andre Szmyt, who connected on a career-long 56-yard field goal. The kick helped secure the victory, and Fannin said he appreciated the pressure that comes with Szmyt’s job.
“Words can even explain it, man. I’m proud of him, you know. People don’t even think about all the stress that goes into it. But every time, he goes out there and does his job. I’m very proud of him, I love him, man, and [I'm] excited to see him do something that great.”
Asked how the Browns will handle the inevitable outside noise, Fannin returned to the same theme of preparation and steady work.
“Just keep coming to work every day ready to work, and you know, don’t settle. Just keep coming to practice and keep working hard.”
The Browns will look to improve their record to 4-1 when they travel to MetLife Stadium next Sunday to face the New York Jets. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET.

title: Browns Went from Disaster to 3-1 as Todd Monken Reveals what Fueled the Turnaround
full_text:
Todd Monken didn’t pretend he saw the Browns’ 3-1 start coming.
“I’m human,” Monken said. “If you said that’s the way we’d start the season after the way we’ve worked, I would’ve said you’re nuts . And if you said we’d be 3-1 after that first game, I’d say you’re nuts, but that’s a credit to our players because all they do is just work. They didn’t blink. That week after was a little chippy, and that was a good thing. They were not happy with the way we played, and sometimes, that’s good.”
That frustration gave Monken something to build on. The Browns weren’t happy with their performance against Jacksonville , and their response showed him how much the work mattered to them.
Cleveland has since found ways to finish close games . Monken noted that the Browns have been on the winning side of three one-score games, while emphasizing that their work is far from finished.
“We’re nowhere near where we want to be or where we’re going to be, but we’ve got the right guys and the right mindset every single day to attack it, which gives you a chance,” he said.
The victory over Pittsburgh offered another example of how Cleveland has handled adversity.
The Browns endured a lengthy opening drive, 14 penalties and multiple turnovers. Denzel Ward’s interception helped change the momentum, giving Cleveland an opportunity to get its offense going.
Monken knows how dangerous it is to leave an experienced quarterback like Aaron Rodgers within striking distance. Even when the Browns built a lead, Pittsburgh kept forcing them to respond.
“But you’re right, the resiliency of our team to keep fighting and to not blink, that’s the bottom, don’t flinch,” Monken said.
He traced that lesson back to his days as a graduate assistant under Lou Holtz at Notre Dame. Nearly four decades later, it still applies.
“Absolutely don’t flinch, and our guys have not flinched,” Monken said.
Still, surviving mistakes doesn’t mean accepting them. Cleveland’s penalties remain a concern, particularly the infractions that happen before the snap.
“And especially the pre-snap penalties, that’s something we control, that’s got nothing to do with them, it’s got everything to do with us,” Monken said.
Monken said he hasn’t deliberately made “believe” the team’s rallying cry . He has emphasized trusting the process, playing physically, giving effort and staying connected.
The belief has developed as players and coaches have watched that work produce results.
“So, when you watch the guys work as hard as they work and connect like they connect with each other, there’s going to be a growing belief in what they’re going to show on tape, every time you take the field,” Monken said.
The coaching staff has had to respond, too. Monken said the Jacksonville game reinforced the need to be aggressive defensively and continue adjusting the scheme.
“We’re always under construction,” he said.
At 3-1, the Browns have given themselves a promising start. Monken’s confidence comes from the way his players return to work, even with plenty left to fix.
“I just think our guys believe in the staff, and the staff believes in them, but then you’ve got to go out there and do it.”

title: The Good, the Bad, the Ugly From Browns Win Over Steelers on TNF
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns moved to 3-1 after beating the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 in a memorable Thursday Night Football showdown.
Here are a few moments from the game that stood out in both good and bad ways:
Watson resembled his former Houston self in several moments, especially in the first half and again at the end of the fourth quarter. He led the Browns on a game-winning drive that ended with a field goal by Andre Szmyt.
The 31-year-old quarterback completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards, with one touchdown, one interception and one lost fumble. Watson needs to address his turnover issues, since both turnovers occurred in the second half and kept the Steelers in the game.
One of the main reasons why the Browns came out with a win was getting Aaron Rodgers on the ground. The Browns recorded five sacks, with five players each getting one. Maliek Collins, Mike Hall, Sam Williams, Isaiah McGuire and Adin Huntington.
The Browns' defensive line quickly pressured Rodgers, and even when they didn't sack him, they still applied enough pressure to force incomplete passes.
It's hard to find negatives when the Browns beat the Steelers, but the biggest concern is the injury that defensive tackle Mason Graham sustained in the first half. Graham has been the best defensive player heading into the Week 4 matchup against the Steelers, with four sacks this season. Unfortunately, he will miss time due to the injury.
The good news is that Graham did not suffer a season -ending injury. The Browns reported on Friday that he has an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain, and he will be week-to-week as he recovers.
It's brutal to see Graham miss time, as he looked like one of the best defensive tackles in the NFL so early in his second NFL season.
The Browns are finding a way to win games, even though they can't always avoid penalties. Cleveland had 14 accepted penalties against them on Thursday, and that doesn't even count a few penalties the Steelers declined. One play in the first quarter saw three penalties on the Browns' defense.
Cleveland needs to address its penalty issues, as it may start to catch up to the Browns. Penalties almost cost the Browns in the last two weeks, and while they didn't lose, it will become a problem soon if they aren't careful.

title: The Browns Are Winning, but One Concerning Issue Must Get Fixed ASAP
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are the talk of the town after beating the Steelers in dramatic fashion last Thursday night for a 27-24 victory that leaves them all alone at the top of the AFC North rankings, at least until the Ravens and Bengals play on Sunday.
Head coach Todd Monken’s group showed good intensity throughout the matchup, and the Browns being able to muster a game-winning drive with a little over a minute and a half to go speaks volumes on where this team is mentally at the moment.
However, there is one concerning issue with Cleveland’s play that might get lost among all the hoopla over the club’s 3-1 record, and failing to address it can certainly lead to a sudden crash and burn.
Penalties threatened to wipe out the Browns’ victory last night.
For the game, Cleveland was penalized a whopping 14 times for 88 yards, versus  eight penalties for 50 yards against the Steelers. However, those numbers don’t even begin to tell the whole story.
The two most obvious miscues came late in the game, aiding Pittsburgh in their game-tying drive inside the final two-minute warning. Down by 8 and after two straight incomplete passes from Aaron Rodgers to Darnell Washington -- both broken up by safety Ronnie Hickman -- on second-and-10 and third-and-10 from the Cleveland 11-yard line, rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was lineup on Washington on fourth-and-10, committing a defensive pass interference that led to Pittsburgh scoring on the very next play, a first-and-goal from the 3 on a pass from Rodgers to Pat Freiermuth.
Defensive end Jared Verse made everything worse on the ensuing 2-point try by committing an egregious defensive offsides that put the Steelers just a yard and a half away from the goal line, with Rodgers converting on a QB sneak to tie it up.
Earlier, though, the Browns had also helped Pittsburgh find some points. On the Steelers last drive of the first half, an illegal hands to face penalty on Sam Williams negated a 6-yard sack by Adin Huntington on first-and-10 on the Cleveland 18. The play before that was an incomplete pass that got negated due to an illegal use of hands on cornerback Myles Harden against Roman Wilson on first-and-10 from the 23. That drive ended eventually with a short Pittsburgh field goal, cutting the distance to 21-10.
And on the very first scoring drive of the game, on third-and-16 around midfield, the Browns handed the Steelers 15 yards and a fresh set of downs thanks to a roughing the passer penalty on Maliek Collins that, otherwise, would have ended in a punt since the Steelers only gained 9 yards on a pass play. That led to Roman Wilson’s 12-yard score in the first quarter.
On the offensive side, an offensive holding on Harden during a punt return by KC Concepcion in the third backed the Browns all the way to their 4, and a false start by the rookie wideout on third-and-8 a few plays later doomed the drive.
Cleveland’s lack of discipline was also on display on two plays that weren’t flagged but should have, marking potentially a 10-point swing.
In the second quarter, on the Steelers’ missed Chris Boswell field goal from 48-yards out, Verse could have easily been penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct after striking/pushing the opponent after the failed kick. That would have resulted in a 15-yard gain and an automatic first down which, in all likelihood, might have led to another field goal try from a shorter distance or a touchdown.
On the Browns’ next drive, capped off with a Deshaun Watson to Harold Fannin 2-yard touchdown pass, right tackle Tytus Howard’s right leg starts to move just as T.J. Watt is starting to take off. Howard isn’t flagged but Watt is, meaning the touchdown stood. If Watt actually provoked Howard to move first, then the play should have been whistled dead and the ball moved closer to the goal line. If Howard moved first, then the Browns should have brought the ball back 5-yards for the false start. In any case, the officials didn’t seem to notice Howard’s movement, but they should have.
With one more game played than almost everyone else, Cleveland leads the NFL in enforced penalties , clearing the second-place Packers by 11 after Thursday night’s game. Nobody has more false start (10), defensive holding (9) or roughing the passer penalties (3) than the Browns so far, according to The Football Database.
The Browns are eking out wins and that always supersedes everything. But the team is playing far from perfect, and leaving these penalties issues unattended will undoubtedly lead to losses .

title: Why Deshaun Watson's Success Through Four Weeks Puts Browns in Difficult Spot
full_text:
After the Browns' 27-24 win on Thursday Night Football against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Deshaun Watson is putting the Browns organization in a tough spot.
Coming into the season and especially after the poor week one performance , many Browns fans thought Deshaun Watson would play his last game for Cleveland against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2.
That was until Watson somehow turned back the clock.
Since losing to the Jaguars by 24 points, Watson has not only led the Browns to three straight wins, but also to three straight game-winning drives.
🎯 pic.twitter.com/oY6U9Buohb
With the way Deshaun Watson is playing right now, you can't take him off of the field.
Simply put, he is doing things the Browns have dreamed of since losing Baker Mayfield , like running the offense and winning games.
But what if he keeps up this production?
Watson currently has 855 passing yards, six touchdowns, and two interceptions through the first four games.
Don't forget he is in the final year of his historic five-year, $230 million contract as well. If the Browns can find success with Watson at the helm, it almost feels like they have to re-sign him.
At this rate of production and winning, combined with the weakest strength of schedule out of all 32 teams in the NFL, who is to say this team can't make the playoffs?
When Watson was named the starting quarterback, fans were counting down the days until Shedeur Sanders would make his start.
But now that Watson is winning games and putting up numbers, the Browns really don't need the Colorado product at the current moment.
This is where they could make a big mistake.
There have been rumors swirling around about other teams in the league reaching out in regards to a potential Sanders trade. If the Browns let him go, there won't be depth at the most important position anymore.
The past five years for the Cleveland Browns have not been pretty, so why is it all suddenly coming together now?
There is one man who has both revived Watson's career and reignited the fire across the depth chart, Todd Monken .
Since the Browns brought in their new coach, he has done a fantastic job making Watson's job easy. Monken has been calling simple passing plays and letting young playmakers like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion make the plays rather than relying on Watson to push the ball down the field constantly.
Because of this style, Watson has been able to find that former Texans self who can play freely but has confident plays to fall back on.
Since the Browns began their winning ways three weeks ago, the culture has shifted for the Brown and Orange.
The team isn't giving up late in games when production cools down like they used to. Guys aren't playing for a coach who doesn't fire them up.
Most importantly, they are rallying behind number four.

title: Biggest Winners and Losers From Browns Win Against Steelers on TNF
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have turned the NFL upside down and improved to 3-1 on the young season.
After a quarter of the season, they sit alone at the top of the AFC North after beating the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football.
Much like the season as a whole, Thursday’s game had its ups, downs, and everything in between.
On a night where there were plenty of winners, there were also some under performers as well:
Watson had his best first half of football in a Browns uniform. The offense rattled off 21 points in the second quarter and opened up a multi-score lead. He stalled out in the second half, but did lead the offense to two field goals in the final half of the fourth quarter. There was a strip sack and an interception that helped the Steelers mount a comeback.
Watson took a bad sack on the last drive that could have resulted in the Browns being out of field goal range, but Andre Szmyt walloped a game-winning 56-yard field goal.
He finished with 268 yards passing , which is a season high. His touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. was placed perfectly and he pushed the ball downfield.
Watson used his legs to buy time and although he missed a handful of easy passes, he made the plays when he needed to, yet again.
There was a lot of hype for Verse’s addition to the Browns’ defense in the offseason.
He has yet to record a sack on the young season and he had his worst game as a Brown on Thursday night. Verse only recorded two tackles, but one of those was for a loss.
He committed an unnecessary penalty that extended a Steelers drive and kept a tired defense on the field.
The second-round rookie has been the most reliable playmaker on the Browns’ offense. He had four catches for 89 yards. Boston has made big play after big play. He averaged more than 20 yards a catch, highlighted by his 60-yard reception early in the second quarter.
He has made the plays when his number has been called and his big-play ability stands out.
The talk leading into the game was that the Browns had to limit their penalties in order to win the game. They committed 14 infractions in the game for 88 yards.
The Steelers had a lengthy first drive that resulted in their only first-half points, which only happened because of the penalties.
For as good as Ward has been throughout his career, he does not get many interceptions because teams just avoid throwing his way in general.
Ward picked the ball off at a time when the team needed a spark. From that moment on, the Browns played with their backside on fire and opened up a double-digit lead.
The running game has yet to be an effective asset on offense. Judkins averaged 3.1 yards per carry.
It was not a poor performance, but the Browns needed a more productive running game to take the pressure off of Watson and the receivers.
Perfection is the only word to describe Szmyt’s season so far.
He made all five of his kicks, which included a game-winning 56-yard field goal. The kick was never in doubt and would have been good from probably 60+ yards.
"I knew it was money . He told me the landmark, so he was just lining it up, and we see it all the time,"  Watson said of Szmyt's attitude on the last drive.
Remember him? Jeudy’s lack of production moved him down to the third and sometimes the fourth receiver on the depth chart.
He hauled in three catches for 36 yards in the win. Jeudy made an incredible contested catch in a crucial moment. The defender was celebrating an incomplete pass, while Jeudy held the ball and gestured for a first down.
On a night where the Browns won their third-straight game and gained sole possession of first place, there were no true losers.
And honestly, the biggest winner of the night was the Browns’ fans that stayed up late and celebrated the victory.

title: Official Update Released on Mason Graham's Injury Suffered in Browns Win Thursday
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a better understanding of defensive tackle Mason Graham's recent injury.
On Thursday, Oct. 1, Browns standout Graham went down with a lower-body injury after being blocked into a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers' offensive line. His left leg bent awkwardly. Immediately, it was apparent that the 23-year-old was in a heap of pain.
He was later ushered out of the stadium in a brace and using crutches.
While most of Friday morning was spent speculating what was going on with Graham and how bad his injury would end up being, NFL Insider Ian Rapoport put the questions to rest.
Around 12:30 p.m. EST on Friday, Rapoport confirmed that Graham would be out for a few weeks with an MLC sprain and an ankle sprain based on preliminary evaluations.
#Browns DL Mason Graham, a standout who leads the team in sacks, is expected to miss a few weeks with an MCL sprain and ankle sprain, sources say based on the preliminary evaluation. The MRI revealed some good news, with hopes that it’s not a long-term injury. pic.twitter.com/rDwZFWGS3Q
According to various sources, a Grade 1 MCL sprain can allow athletes to return to the field in roughly one to two weeks, while a Grade 2 sprain requires two to four weeks of rehabilitation. Ankle injuries are in that same window, as some can heal within days while others could be a weeks-long process as well.
As more testing is done, Graham's official timeline will begin to take shape.
While Cleveland is going to have to make major adjustments with Graham being out, especially considering he had posted 15 tackles, six for a loss, five quarterback hits and four sacks across the first three games, his not being out for the season or having to undergo some sort of surgery is a major positive to the situation.
The No. 5 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, Graham, put together a strong rookie campaign, recording 49 tackles, seven for a loss and eight quarterback hits.
Seeing such a major jump in his productivity in the sack column from his rookie campaign to his sophomore season had him on pace to be in the conversation as one of the league's most impactful defensive linemen, and while he likely won't finish at the top of the stat sheet due to being out for a few weeks, he has already established himself as one of the league's most intriguing youngsters when healthy.
Taking Graham's place will be a combination of Mike Hall Jr., Adin Huntington and Maliek Collins, while edge rushers Sam Williams and Derek Barnett likely take a few snaps inside if no external moves are made.
In the meantime, the Browns will look to keep their current momentum going , being winners of their last three outings.
Set to travel to New York next weekend, the Browns will square off against the Jets at 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Oct. 11.

title: Browns Receive Huge Mason Graham Injury News After Thursday Night Scare
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns battled to take down the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Thursday night.
And even with standout defensive tackle Mason Graham going down early in the outing with a lower-body injury, the defense stayed on the attack, sacking future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers a whopping five times.
Graham's importance to the team cannot be overstated , especially with how hot a season he has been having up until this point. After he exited, the team knew how important it would be to fill his void, with counterpart Mike Hall Jr. speaking to such a sentiment postgame.
"The situation was just bigger," Hall Jr. said about fighting through his own injury to stay in the game for the defense. "You know, just bigger than me. I have already dealt with adversity with my knee last year, so you know, just coming off this ankle, it was only two d-tackles left. I didn't want to leave my brothers out there."
When Mason Graham went down with a knee injury, the #Browns turned to Mike Hall Jr., but then he suffered an ankle injury. Hall pushed through and returned to the game...then got a sack. He said the moment was bigger than him. But will he be good to go? "Oh hell yeah." pic.twitter.com/rQ4Fyr5uS9
Hall Jr. finished the night with a sack, while Adin Huntington, Maliek Collins, Isaiah McGuire and Sam Williams each grabbed one as well.
Hoping for good news from Graham's medical evaluations on Friday morning, head coach Todd Monken shared that the Browns are still in limbo. He said that he does not yet have an update and that an MRI is to be done at some point.
Just minutes prior to Monken's comments, Ian Rapoport announced that the early belief is that Graham "dodged a bullet" and does not have a significant knee injury.
However, with no official medical confirmation, that is still a possibility.
Graham left the stadium Thursday night in a knee brace and on crutches after being blocked into a Steelers lineman.
Through the first four games of the campaign, Graham has eight total tackles, four sacks and five quarterback hits. He also has six tackles for a loss.
The “early belief” is that Browns DT Mason Graham dodged a bullet and does NOT have a significant knee injury per @RapSheet #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/vUhP9Q6sqW
If the Browns can avoid losing Graham for the entire season, that will be a major positive for the team, especially with edge rusher Jared Verse still trying to settle in with his new team.
Graham has established himself as the prominent leader on the line , and his absence would be a big hit to a surging team.
Mason Graham (94) has been performing well through 2 weeks. pic.twitter.com/9jHSQqjNKT
The Browns will await confirmation on Graham's future as they begin preparing for the New York Jets. The two sides clash at 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Oct. 11, from MetLife Stadium.

title: Will Joey Porter Jr Start For Cowboys In Week 4 vs Texans? Latest On Dallas Debut
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are looking to get back into the win column in Week 4, with a trip to NRG Stadium to face off against the Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon .
One of the biggest questions entering the game is the status of star cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was landed in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this week .
Porter has been battling a back injury that kept him out of training camp and the first three weeks of the season, but a "miraculous recovery" has the cornerback trending toward making his season debut with Dallas.
From @SportsCenter : The very latest on Joey Porter Jr, along with updates on the QB situations for the #Commanders , #Bears , and #Ravens . pic.twitter.com/NAZwTbIEaP
Earlier in the week, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer hinted that Porter would make his debut on Sunday , despite being ruled out for Thursday's game when he was still a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers.
“We’ll see how he moves around today, see if he’s sore today. But I thought it was a great start yesterday," Schottenheimer said at the time. "Really, really pleased with not just what I saw on the field, but really just the way he attacked his preparation and in learning the system. The big thing that will drive this is his ability to communicate with Caleb Downs and some of the safeties and things like that as we get ready to finish the prep.”
Now, we know that he is set to take the field when the Cowboys take on the Texans in a matter of hours.
Joey Porter Jr. is set to play for the Dallas Cowboys days after being traded from Pittsburgh, but the team is expected to limit his snaps vs Houston. One source estimated about 30 snaps or so, depending on the flow of the game.
Last season, Porter had the most snaps without allowing a touchdown, ranked third in passer rating allowed, tied for third in forced incompletions, and was sixth in completion rate allowed.
His debut in Dallas comes at a perfect time, after the team has been struggling with a massive string of injuries to the defensive backfield. Now, Porter gives the team another reliable player on the field, despite likely being limited in snaps.
Dallas wants to bring Porter along slowly as he gets back up to speed after missing the first few games of the season, so we'll have to see just how big of an impact he is able to make. Regardless of whether Porter jumps off the screen in Week 4, he will make the defense a better overall unit in the long run, which is all that Christian Parker can ask for.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 4: George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb
full_text:
Before the start of the 2026 season, there was some debate about who the Dallas Cowboys' No. 1 wide receiver was between George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb.
That's because Pickens had a career-best showing in 2025 while Lamb finished second on the team in receiving yards during what was an injury-plagued campaign for him.
Fast forward to 2026 and Lamb has been far and away the No. 1 wide receiver in Dallas. He leads the team in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns through three games. Meanwhile, Pickens has been OK, but nowhere near how dominant he was last season.
As we turn the page to Week 4, here's how we're handling start or sit decisions with Lamb and Pickens against the Houston Texans.
Pickens is coming off his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign after he notched season-highs with seven receptions and 82 yards. However, Pickens has yet to find the end zone.
It has been a disappointing season overall for the fifth-year wide receiver after he was an elite option last season, but he still ranks as WR23 overall, according to Fantasy Pros , which keeps him on the flex map.
We're now heading into Week 4, which was the same week in which Pickens started to really get going last season, when he ripped off eight catches for 134 yards and two touchdowns. It is worth noting, however, Lamb sat that game out.
Despite having a supremely talented secondary, the group has not lived up to its billing through three contests, with the Texans permitting the third-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
Pickens is a starter in Week 4.
Lamb has been sensational the past two weeks with 15 catches for 265 yards and two scores, which leaves him ranked as WR3 overall.
In no world are you sitting Lamb in any week, and that's even more so true in Week 4 in a matchup against a Texans defense that has permitted the third-most fantasy points per game to the position.
Maybe Houston's struggling pass defense finally finds its way this week, but this isn't exactly a get-right spot with Lamb and Pickens rolling through Reliant Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 4: Dak Prescott, Jake Ferguson, Javonte Williams
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams had a much better fantasy football showing in Week 3 than his teammates, tight end Jake Ferguson and quarterback Dak Prescott.
Williams posted a top-10 showing at his position last week, but both Prescott and Ferguson ranked outside the top 15, which amounted to a surprise in a game that finished 34-31 .
Looking ahead to Week 4, when the Cowboys take on the Houston Texans, here's our fantasy football start or sit advice for all three players.
Williams finally got going on the ground last week, with the veteran back rushing for a season-high 98 yards, and he found the end zone, too. With that performance, Williams now ranks as RB11 overall, per Fantasy Pros , which makes him an RB2.
This matchup against the Texans is a bad one, though, as Houston is ceding the third-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, per CBS Sports , and the fifth-fewest rushing yards.
That said, his overall ranking and his expected volume is enough to keep Williams in lineups, although temper expectations to flex production this week.
Prescott ranks as QB7 overall, which makes him an every-week starting option in 10-team leagues.
Houston's defense has a load of talent in the secondary and along the defensive line, yet the Texans are surrendering the 10th-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, and the seventh-most passing yards per game in general.
We're expecting the switch to flip against the pass at some point for such a talented defense, but because we haven't seen that through three games, we're starting Prescott in Week 4.
We believed Ferguson would regress in the scoring department this season after he had a career-high eight touchdowns in 2025. However, through three games, it doesn't look like that'll happen because Ferguson has found pay dirt three times already. That remains the biggest reason why Ferguson is ranked as TE14.
The Texans have amounted to a middle-of-the-road matchup versus tight ends in terms of fantasy points allowed, although Houston hasn't given up a score to the position yet.
We're no doubt concerned about Ferguson's ability to rack up the kind of receiving totals needed to turn in an adequate showing in fantasy without a touchdown, but Ferguson has just barely been good enough this season to keep him in lineups this week, especially considering how shallow the position can be.

title: Caleb Downs Reveals Truth About Field Conditions In Dallas Cowboys' Rio Game
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys lost a 34-31 heartbreaker to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil last week, falling to 1-2 in the process.
The thrilling finish almost made everyone forget about the conversation that dominated the headlines in the days leading up to kickoff. Concerns about the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium in Rio De Janeiro was all anyone could talk about, so much so that the NFL even had a representative speak with the media a day before the game to ensure that everything met league standards.
Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs talked about the field conditions during a recent podcast episode of Downs 2 Business, and he didn't hold back his honest thoughts on Maracanã Stadium.
Downs admitted that the field conditions at Maracanã Stadium started off fine but eventually got worse as the game went on.
"It was okay at the beginning of the game honestly," Downs said. "We had prepared that week, a lot of us practiced in seven studs just making sure we were ready. So even with that, at the end of the game, we was still slipping out there, and I’m like ‘Bro this is terrible.’” But it was what it was and you can’t make any excuses about it because they had to play on it too."
As Downs said, field conditions aside, the Cowboys can't use that as an excuse for how the game ended. Slippery and unstable grass had nothing to do with the game-losing defensive call by Christian Parker on the second-to-last play that allowed the Ravens to get into field goal range for kicker Tyler Loop, who nailed the game-winning 56-yarder as time expired.
It certainly didn't appear to have an impact on the Dallas defense in some crucial moments earlier in the contest before the team's eventual collapse. Despite the loss, the Cowboys' defense stepped up with some of its best plays through three weeks of action.
Downs and his fellow rookie star Jaishawn Barham came up big on some impressive short-yardage stops against Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry and the talented Ravens offense.
Downs finished the game with three total tackles (two solo) while Barham had seven total tackles and two tackles for loss.
The rookie duo will look to build off their promising performance in Brazil when the Cowboys visit the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on Sunday at 12 p.m. CT.

title: Cowboys Elevate Newly-Signed DB for Week 4 vs. Texans
full_text:
In need of help in the secondary, the Dallas Cowboys unsurprisingly elevated two players from the practice squad for their Week 4 contest against the Houston Texans . With multiple players dealing with injuries, the Cowboys will add cornerback Reddy Steward and safety Juanyeh Thomas to their game-day roster.
For Steward, this will be the second week in a row he's been activated. Last week, he helped fill in after Cobie Durant was ruled out with a hamstring injury . With Durant out of action again in Week 4, Steward will get the call.
Steward is in his second season with the Cowboys and earned plenty of praise from fans last year. Despite being on a defense that struggled mightily, Steward continually showed off plenty of grit and had 63 tackles, 1.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, and three pass defenses. He was at his best in the slot, but when asked to expand his role against the Ravens in Week 3, Steward struggled and was one of the lower-rated players on the team during the loss.
At safety, the Cowboys were thin as well entering the game against Baltimore with Malik Hooker and P.J. Locke both out. Their depth was challenged even more when Jalen Thompson was injured during the game . With him out, Alijah Clark was given an opportunity, but Dallas had no more depth to lean on.
That led to Thomas reaching out via social media, saying he was ready to help . The Cowboys were in agreement that a reunion with Thomas was a good idea, signing him to the practice squad as they prepared for the game against the Texans. Now just a few days later, Thomas will be active and could end up with a significant role for Dallas.
The Cowboys are hopeful that Hooker can return, but even if he does, they might not be willing to let him go full speed. As for the safeties they know will suit up, Dallas is down to Markquese Bell and Clark. Caleb Downs is an option as well, but he's better suited in the slot.
Thomas, a former undrafted free agent out of Georgia Tech, has 62 tackles, five pass defenses, and a forced fumble in 36 career games with four starts. He's also known as a special teams ace, even recording a kick return for a touchdown in 2024.

title: Dallas Cowboys Should Have Eyes on Rumored Pittsburgh Steelers Trade Candidate
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' pass-rush has been an utter disaster over the first three weeks of the season, and that should have the Cowboys searching for more help at the position.
The Cowboys have posted 43 pressures thus far , but they have only turned two of those into sacks. Making matters worse, the only edge rusher with a sack is Donovan Ezeiruaku with 0.5.
The Athletic's Jonathan Jones recently put together a list of trade candidates based on what he's hearing from executives around the NFL.
Among them was Pittsburgh Steelers edge rusher Alex Highsmith.
"After shaking down sources this week, I’m keeping an eye on a number of players," Jones wrote before listing Highsmith as one of six players he's watching moving forward.
We don't see the Steelers trading Highsmith right now, but if the Steelers are in a precarious spot at the trade deadline, which is possible considering how uneven the Steelers have looked through four games.
That's because Highsmith will be in the final year of his contract in 2027. Sure, the Steelers could opt to unload him then, but trading Highsmith now will allow Pittsburgh to get more value because he can contribute to a team for more than one season, assuming the acquiring team doesn't extend him.
There stands a chance the Steelers could extend Highsmith, but with the money Pittsburgh is paying both T.J. Watt and Nick Herbig, who was extended this offseason, that isn't likely.
The Steelers and Cowboys have pulled off three significant trades in recent years, with George Pickens, Broderick Jones and Joey Porter Jr. being the centerpiece of each.
These two teams clearly like doing business with one another and the Cowboys could certainly use a proven edge rusher like Highsmith given their putrid situation currently.
Highsmith already has three sacks this season, which is more than the Cowboys have as a team. Highsmith is also coming off a 9.5-sack season that is made more impressive by the fact that he missed four games due to injury.
Highsmith would instantly be the best edge rusher on Dallas' roster upon his arrival.
When it comes to compensation, we could see Highsmith fetching at least one third-round pick after Jonathan Greenard returned two for the Minnesota Vikings in the trade with the Philadelphia Eagles, and that was with Greenard needing a new deal.
The Cowboys are extremely low on future draft picks , with Dallas having just four in 2027, none of which come in the third round. However, the Cowboys do have Pittsburgh's fourth, so maybe Dallas can package that with another pick.
There is also the 2028 stable that includes a pick in every round but the second and seventh.
Trading more draft capital might not seem feasible, but owner Jerry Jones has said he's open to doing more to improve the defense, even after the Porter trade.
If things keep up the way they have with the Cowboys' pass-rush come the trade deadline, we could see Dallas pulling the trigger on a trade for Highsmith or any other impact edge rusher available.

title: Dallas Cowboys Might Not See Micah Parsons in Week 6 vs. Packers After All
full_text:
Before the season started, reports suggested that Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons could return from injury in Week 6.
That was not only significant because it gave the Packers a clear target for when they might get their start player back from his torn ACL, but it is also the week the Packers play the Dallas Cowboys , which would only add more juice to Parsons' return.
However, as it turns out, a showdown between Parsons and his former team at Lambeau may not happen after all.
According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , not only could Parsons not be ready to go by Week 6, he may not be ready to play until November.
"Packers star Micah Parsons hasn’t had any setbacks in his rehab," Pelissero reported. "But he’s not expected to practice next week, and it could be November before he’s ready for game action."
Bear in mind, Dallas and Green Bay's matchup falls on Oct. 18 , so that's at least two weeks added to Parsons' timeline. If he doesn't play until November, that means Parsons will miss at least half the season depending on how late into November he gets back.
Just a few days ago, Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said the team would be cautious with Parsons because of the big investement the team made in him, both with the trade and his monster contract extension.
Gutekunst indicated that, at the four-week mark, Parsons would be "pretty close" to returning.
"We have a pretty good idea, once we get out of that four-game window, that we’re going to be pretty close," Gutekunst said, according to The Athletic's Matt Schneidman .
"As you guys have heard me say, I’m going to be pretty cautious with that. We’ve got a big investment there. It’s really important to what we’re trying to do. To accomplish the goals we want to late in the year, he’s going to need to be at his best," he added.
While the Packers are wise to be cautious with Parsons, they are also in desperate need of the kind of jolt he can provide given the horrific start the team is off to.
For their part, the Packers gave up two first-round picks and Kenny Clark for 14 games of Parsons thus far.
The Cowboys ultimately turned that trade into Clark, Quinnen Williams, who was acquired in part with one of Dallas' two first-rounders, and Malachi Lawrence, Devin Moore and LT Overton, with the three rookies being drafted with the picks acquired in Dallas' move back out of Green Bay's 2026 first-round pick.
Unfortunately for Dallas, none of those players have really panned out thus far. Clark hasn't done much, Williams has been mostly disappointing, and the three rookies have contributed little to nothing over three games.
Of course, it is still early in the season for all five of those players, but so far this trade isn't looking all that great for either team.

title: Cowboys Pass on Arch Manning, Opt For George Pickens Replacement in NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
If the Dallas Cowboys were staring down the option of taking Texas quarterback Arch Manning in the 2027 NFL Draft, would owner Jerry Jones be able to pass up on taking him?
We couldn't say for sure, even with Dak Prescott on the team. That's because Prescott is getting up there in age at 33, and in price, and Jones loves himself a good splash and drafting a Manning would certainly qualify as such.
The Manning scenario played out in the latest mock draft from Athlon Sports' Luke Easterling. He has the Cowboys with the No. 8 pick and Manning is on the board when Dallas is up in that spot.
However, Easterling has the Cowboys going for Indiana wideout Charlie Becker instead. Manning, meanwhile, goes to Cleveland with the No. 15 overall pick.
Easterling believes the Cowboys won't want to extend Pickens, which will lead to Dallas drafting Backer as his replacement.
"I don’t expect the Cowboys to pay top dollar to keep George Pickens as their WR2 across from CeeDee Lamb, and if he ends up leaving in the offseason, they’ll need a capable replacement," Easterling wrote.
We tend to agree with Easterling about Pickens. The Cowboys will have bigger fish to fry and it just doesn't make much sense to pay a massive sum of money to yet another receiver.
Even co-owner Stephen Jones has hinted that backing up the Brinks truck for Pickens may not be feasible .
"The situation we have with George Pickens going alongside CeeDee.. I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said. "So, yeah. That's going to be a real difficult situation as we move forward. We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year.
"Certainly, if everything works out the way we think it is, which CeeDee and George both have huge years again, then it'll be a bigger challenge next year. George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it'll help his market. And certainly I know at some point, as does every player in this league, will want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there."
Here's more on Becker, per Easterling:
"Becker brings an impressive blend of size (6-4, 208) and athleticism to the table, with the hands and body control to win contested-catch situations, along with a knack for making big plays in clutch moments," Easterling said.
Becker posted 34 catches for 679 yards and four touchdowns last season, and he ripped off a whopping 20 yards per reception, which shows his big-play ability.
Becker is on pace to smash those numbers in 2026, as he's already up to 19 catches for 370 yards and six scores in four contests this season.
If he stays on that pace, it won't be a question of Becker being a first-round pick, but rather how high he goes in the first round.
The Cowboys would be wise to opt for a receiver in the 2027 draft if Pickens departs. Becker would be a fine option to replace him and would allow Dallas to allocate its resources elsewhere.

title: Cowboys' Trade With Steelers for Joey Porter Jr. Not Viewed Favorably By NFL Peers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys went out and got the player they needed in Joey Porter Jr. via trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers .
The Cowboys ended up giving up a second-round pick and a sixth-round selection for the veteran cornerback, who will now look to help Dallas solve its coverage woes on defense.
But did the Cowboys overpay for Porter? Well, there are "many around the league" who believe Dallas did, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones .
"Many around the league believed Dallas overpaid, based largely on the belief that teams don’t view Porter as a top-tier corner," Jones reported.
“They were bidding against themselves for Porter,” one unnamed executive told Jones.
The general consensus seems to be that while Porter is a very good player, he isn't among the elite of the elite, and Pittsburgh might share that belief after its reluctance to pay him the big money Porter was seeking in an extension.
While the executive said the Cowboys were bidding against themselves, that doesn't appear to be accurate. We know there was at least one other team in the running for Porter after Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell admitted the team was talking to Pittsburgh about a deal. It isn't clear what the Lions were offering.
"We were very much in on him," Campbell told reporters.
It isn't clear what the Lions were offering.
One NFL general manager who spoke to Jones considered it a fair trade because he views the 2028 second-round pick as equal to a 2027 third-rounder, which makes the compensation "down the fairway."
"This is a view held by many — but not all — across the league: a future pick is discounted against a current one," Jones said.
When viewed through that lens, it's a very good deal for Dallas.
Even if you don't think Porter isn't among the best of the best at his position, he is certainly a good No. 1 corner and what the Cowboys gave up is fair value, at worst.
Porter still doesn't have a contract and the veteran cornerback has said he will bet on himself in Dallas and play without one.
“Bet on myself. You got to always have that at the end of the day, and that’s what I’m doing,” Porter said.
While that solves the issue for now, the Cowboys are going to have to address Porter's contract next offseason. How Dallas approaches that will depend on what Porter puts on tape.
If he's the impact player Dallas was hoping for, the Cowboys are going to try and extend him , or franchise tag him if the two sides can't agree on compensation before that deadline.
The latter approach might lead to Porter holding out, but we can't say he'll take that route for sure. If that happens, Dallas will no doubt explore a sign-and-trade scenario.
One potential dilemma with the tag is the Cowboys have to weigh saving it for George Pickens, who is eligible to get it again, although at a higher price.
If, for whatever reason, the Cowboys let Porter walk in free agency, the team would likely collect a compensatory pick, something Dallas factored into the equation upon trading for Porter on Wednesday night.

title: Jerry Jones' Word Salad On Cowboys' Lackluster Pass-Rush Sounds Like a Major Cope
full_text:
One area the Dallas Cowboys were hoping to improve with all of their moves in 2026 was the pass-rush.
Dallas' 2025 pass-rush struggled badly, with the team posting just 35 sacks, tied for the seventh-fewest in the NFL.
Well, things have been worse in 2026, with the Cowboys posting just two sacks in three games, the third-fewest in the NFL. That puts Dallas on pace to finish with even less sacks than it did in 2025.
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones touched on the subject during his latest interview on 105.3 The Fan on Friday and sounded like he's trying to cope with the fact that the resources the team dumped into the pass-rush, which included the trade for Rashan Gary , the draft selection of Malachi Lawrence and the signing of Von Miller , hasn't panned out at all.
“What you’re seeing is a pursuit of and a goal of having the closing part of the pass rush. Actually getting the sacks," he stated . "What you’re seeing is let’s do that and pursue that and at the same time check the run first … and earn the right to get a pass rush.
“What you’re seeing is a real effort to get that balance as close as we can with very competent players.”
The Cowboys' attempt at finding that balance has failed miserably, as the Cowboys sport the second-worst run defense in the NFL.
The Cowboys have been getting decent pressure, with 43 over the first three games, according to Pro Football Focus , but Dallas just hasn't been able to get home. What's more frustrating is the fact that the Cowboys have only gotten a half of a sack from their EDGE group, with that coming from Donovan Ezeiruaku.
Meanwhile, Miller, Gary and Lawrence have combined for 13 pressures but no sacks. Gary in particular has not taken the quarterback down since Week 8 of last season.
This issue is even more glaring when you consider just how poorly the Cowboys have covered pass-catchers. That's not all the fault of the pass-rush, but the inability to sack the quarterback has no doubt played at least a sizeable role.
While Dallas will likely have to wait for an opportunity to add to the group, at least the team was able to acquire Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night.
The Cowboys can only hope Porter's presence improves the coverage and aids the pass-rush with more time to get home. Porter might be able to do that as soon as this week, as it looks like he'll play against the Houston Texans.
If Porter doesn't make that kind of impact, it's might continue to be nothing but pain for the Cowboys' pass defense, which has been woefully disappointing.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for How Broncos Can Take Down 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been the NFL's best team through three weeks, and it isn't all that close. The Denver Broncos have to face them on Sunday.
To add to the difficulty, the Broncos won't have home-field advantage, and they'll be playing in potentially record temperatures at Levi's Stadium. That puts the onus on a few players to deliver elite performances and puts pressure on the team to play its best overall this season.
This week's bold predictions factor all of this in. Nailing these would all but guarantee a win. Let's dive in.
Denver ranks 11th in overall explosive play rate on offense, 20th in rushing, and eighth in passing, while the 49ers' defense ranks first overall, first in rushing, and third in passing for the lowest explosive play rate allowed.
It is difficult to find explosives against the 49ers, but the Broncos manage to produce eight, with three runs over 10 yards and five passing plays over 20. J.K. Dobbins and Jaylen Waddle need to step up in this one.
There is growing concern about the Broncos' run game because their blocking has been an issue across the board.
The Broncos need to find a way to build a reliable run game. Despite the 49ers' strong run defense, the Broncos run the ball efficiently, averaging at least five yards per rush, with Dobbins and RJ Harvey leading the way.
There may not be a better overall playmaker in the NFL than McCaffrey, given what he can do as a runner and receiver. That said, he has yet to break 120 scrimmage yards this season, with a single game over 100, but the Broncos have had serious issues handling running backs.
The McCaffrey threat will draw attention his way, but the Broncos will be ready for it. Denver emerges with its best day handing a running back so far this season.
Few teams can shut down McCaffrey and Kittle in the same game, and these two bold predictions see the Broncos do just that.
In the last two games, Kittle has 174 receiving yards, with 82 yards last week, 80 yards the game before that, and only 12 in Week 1. Given what Denver allowed the Los Angeles Rams' tight ends to do, and the attention McCaffrey needs, Kittle could have a big game.
But not this time. The Broncos hold Kittle to under 50 yards.
The 49ers' special teams units have been decent, while the Broncos' units have been great. Denver has an opening here to make some big plays on special teams.
With Marvin Mims Jr. back on the field, Denver manages to bust off a return for a touchdown, adding a defensive touchdown to total 14 points. This helps bridge the gap for the Broncos' offense, allowing them to keep up with the 49ers.

title: Several Broncos on Brink of Major Milestones vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are focused on advancing to 3-1 this week as they travel to take on the San Francisco 49ers .
With the Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders both getting off to a 3-0 start, the Broncos can't afford to drop to 2-2 this week — especially given Denver's schedule through Week 8. Meanwhile, the 49ers are also undefeated, though they've yet to really face an opponent quite like the Broncos, and that includes the Los Angeles Rams, who were jet-lagged in their season-opening game down in Australia.
The Broncos lead the all-time series vs. the 49ers 8-7, but they're 3-5 on the road. Denver would much prefer to leave the greater Bay Area 9-7 all-time against the 49ers than 8-8.
Suffice it to say, winning at Levi's Stadium is the Broncos' top priority, but several individuals have milestones or records on the table this week. Let's highlight what to watch for on Sunday.
Payton needs one win to fully overtake Chuck Knox for the 12th-most regular-season wins among head coaches in NFL history. Payton tied Knox last week in the Broncos' 30-26 win over the Rams.
Payton currently has 186 career wins in the regular season. He can officially scoot past Knox, and set his sights on Dan Reeves at at No. 11 (190 wins) with a victory over the 49ers.
With 123 passing yards, Nix would tie Kyle Orton for the seventh-most passing yards in team history. Last week, Nix joined the late Craig Morton and Jay Cutler as the quarterback with the fifth-most games with multiple passing scores in Broncos history.
Nix gets the chance to continue moving up the Broncos' all-time record books with even a subpar passing performance vs. San Francisco.
Sutton needs just one reception ot tie McCaffrey for the fifth-most catches in Broncos history. Once he passes McCaffrey, the next guy is Lionel Taylor, who sits at No. 4 all-time with 543 career receptions.
From there, it's the holy triumvirate of Broncos pass catchers in the top 3 spots: Rod Smith (849 receptions), Shannon Sharpe (675), and the late, great Demaryius Thomas (665). Sutton currently has 461 career receptions.
If Adkins catches a touchdown pass against the 49ers, he'd become the first undrafted tight end in team history to notch a receiving score in three straight games. He had one in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars and another last week against the Rams.
Adkins has been seeing the field a lot as new Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb implements his multi-tight end vision.
Allen needs just one sack to become the first Broncos defensive lineman since Derek Wolfe (2016) to notch 4.0 sacks within the first four games of a season. Allen has been off to a rip-roaring start, especially as an interior pass rusher.
He leads the Broncos with three sacks thus far. Here's to hoping he makes it four in San Francisco, and does what no one else has this season, and sacks Brock Purdy.
You read that right; Purdy is yet to be sacked this season.
Since we're talking sacks, Bonitto needs just two QB takedowns to reach 40 sacks for his career and become the seventh player in Broncos history to reach that milestone. Von Miller leads the franchise with 110.5 career sacks.
Bonitto is still a ways off from joining Miller's lofty status, but becoming one of the elite seven to reach 40 career sacks in a Broncos uniform will be special. Going against 49ers left tackle Trent Williams won't be easy, but nothing lasting or worth while ever is.
If Lutz makes his first extra point attempt on Sunday, he'll tie Tyler Bass for the second-longest point-after streak since 2015. Lutz has nailed 103 consecutive extra-point tries, and he's looking to extend it even further.
Alas, Lutz missed a field goal last week, but that's its own thing. The streak pertains to extra points.

title: Bo Nix Shares His Thoughts on 49ers QB Brock Purdy
full_text:
Bo Nix and Brock Purdy are about to cross swords for the first time ever.
With the Denver Broncos in the greater Bay Area to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, NFL fans will be treated to the first-ever Nix vs. Purdy showdown. It sounds like Nix has been looking forward to this matchup for some time, as his only previous encounters with Purdy and the 49ers have been in joint practice sessions during training camp or preseason games.
“I met him for the first time last year when we joint [practiced] with them," Nix said of Purdy. "I hear really good things about him, and I know he’s a great guy from what I’ve heard."
They may be opponents on Sunday, but Nix and Purdy are brothers in Christ.
Nix really appreciates Purdy's "witness" and how he expresses his faith as a Christian, using his platform as a famous athlete to advocate for his spiritual beliefs and uplift others. Anyone who follows the Broncos knows that Nix's faith in Jesus Christ is extremely important to him and his family.
Nix's "witness" is more than just words. Within the strictures and limits that the NFL imposes, the Broncos' quarterback draws attention to his Christianity by drawing a cross in Sharpie on his wristbands each game. There was more than one reason Tim Tebow was Nix's favorite quarterback growing up.
"He does a great job with his witness as well," Nix said of Purdy. "I just appreciate that and admire that most about him. I think he uses his platform for much bigger things, as I like to do."
Being criminally underrated is another thing Nix and Purdy have in common. Purdy has been playing lights-out this season, with 789 passing yards and nine touchdowns through the first three games.
Nix hasn't been quite that prolific, passing for 605 yards and four touchdowns thus far, but he's beaten two tough teams on the back of his signature fourth-quarter comebacks. Meanwhile, Purdy is undefeated this season — something Nix and the Broncos will look to change this weekend.
"Obviously, he’s playing really good right now," Nix said of Purdy. "He’s one of those guys, he’s been to a Super Bowl, he’s played in a lot of big games. He’s a really good quarterback in our league, probably a little bit underrated."
As you can see, Nix's "appreciation level" is "really high" when it comes to Purdy. It's going to be fun to see these two young quarterbacks square off at Levi's Stadium on Sunday.
Purdy was the final pick in the 2022 NFL draft out of Iowa State. That year's "Mr. Irrelevant" has outkicked his coverage, going 5-0 as a rookie starter and becoming the first 49ers rookie quarterback to win a playoff game.
After his rookie year, the 49ers leaned into Purdy and cut ties with Jimmy Garoppolo and eventually, Trey Lance. Purdy earned Pro Bowl honors in his second year and led the 49ers to a Super Bowl berth before ultimately coming up short against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Purdy took a step back of sorts in Year 3 as the 49ers struggled. In Year 4, he dealt with injury issues that hampered his playing time, though he went 7-2 as a starter.
Under the direction of 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, Purdy has his offense humming. The 49ers appear to be a juggernaut, though two of their three opponents have been cake-walks.
Purdy hit the NFL like he was shot out of a cannon, making some serious waves that belied his Mr. Irrelevant draft pedigree. Nix hit the ground running when he entered the league, too, winning 24 games in his first two seasons and dethroning the Chiefs as AFC West champs last year — a feat that Purdy no doubt appreciates.
Nix has the Broncos sitting at 2-1 entering Week 4. His first head-to-head with Purdy is sure to be must-see football. It's going to be a hot one at Levi's Stadium, in more ways than one.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Details Growth of Vet Captain D.J. Jones
full_text:
He doesn't get the shine of All-Pros on his side of the ball, like cornerback Patrick Surtain II or edge rusher Nik Bonitto, but veteran defensive lineman D.J. Jones is equally a pillar of a vaunted Denver Broncos defense.
Such is why Jones, now in his fifth season with the Broncos, was chosen as a defensive captain for the 2026 season, along with Surtain, inside linebacker Alex Singleton, and safety Talanoa Hufanga.
On Friday, ahead of Denver's Week 4 matchup at San Francisco , head coach Sean Payton discussed the growth he's witnessed from Jones across nearly a half-decade donning orange and blue.
“He’s a leader. He’s really respected. He’s a smart football player," Payton told reporters. "That’s a tough position to play when you’re down-in and down-out a lot of times getting a double team. He’s an important part of our fabric though I would say on this team.”
Characteristically durable, Jones has appeared in each of the Broncos' first three games this season, notching three combined tackles (one solo) across 102 defensive snaps, helping close the gap for a defensive line that lost John Franklin-Myers in free agency.
More of a run-plugger than pass-rusher, Jones will be crucial to Denver's gameplan against a 3-0 49ers squad featuring star running back Christian McCaffrey, keying the NFL's sixth-best rushing offense.
Coincidentally (or not), Jones is among several former 49ers players who've migrated to the Mile High City in recent years. Also through free agency, the Broncos have added Hufanga and right tackle Mike McGlinchey. Like Jones, they're both starters and core pieces to what could be a championship contender later this fall.
“So I did the list yesterday, and there were like eight," Payton noted Friday. "Not just players obviously, coaches, players, of course D.J., ‘Huf’ (Hufanga). I was in New Orleans. We played [49ers Head Coach] Kyle [Shanahan]’s team twice. D.J. was there. I think he was hurt for one of the games. [Pro Football Hall of Fame Quarterback Drew] Brees got hurt for one of the games. We lost one, won one. Huf wasn’t there yet, but there are a lot of imprints. There are some storylines I’m sure with both the teams. [49ers RB Christian] McCaffrey obviously, his first game [against the Broncos]. All of that is good.”
Jones is the lone player of the three to precede Payton's time in Denver, as he joined a year earlier. But it's clear that general manager George Paton was influenced by the 49ers' success and imported such talent to rebuild a barren roster. Once Payton arrived, the plan was accelerated.
“The tiebreaker goes to make up, and I don’t even know if it’s a tie breaker. I think it starts there," Payton affirmed Friday. "Certainly when they’ve been at bigger programs… You’re visiting with a lot of different people. I think you’re taking all of that into… That has to be elite. That formula has worked.”
