title: Broncos-49ers Weather Forecast Could Present Big Challenges
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will take on the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday in a big Week 4 matchup.
The 49ers are 3-0 while the Broncos are 2-1. However, the Broncos have had some great success at Levi's Stadium, winning their third Lombardi Trophy there in Super Bowl 50.
That was more than a decade ago. Things have changed dramatically for both the Broncos and the 49ers since then.
Entering this Week 4 tilt, the weather could play a bigger role than fans might realize, given that it's taking place in California's often ideal climate. Think again.
Let's take a look at the weather forecast for Sunday's game at Levi's Stadium, via AccuWeather .
Temperatures could threaten the local record of 98 degrees for this time of year. It's going to be very hot out on that grass.
The old Candlestick Park was near the ocean, but the 49ers' new stadium is much further inland. Broncos head coach Sean Payton says he'll have a plan for the heat, regardless.
“The old stadium was by the water, and it could get real cool," Payton said on Friday. "This one’s 45-50 minutes away. We’ll have all the plans in place.”
With it likely to be that hot, the challenge will be to stay hydrated. It's poised to be one sweaty day for the Broncos.
Payton has a lot of experience going against the 49ers' new defensive coordinator. As the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach and Atlanta Falcons defensive coordinator, Morris went toe-to-toe with Payton's New Orleans Saints twice a year for a long time.
Payton knows Morris's scheme and tendencies, and vice versa, so it'll be interesting to see whether it serves the Broncos' offense on Sunday.
“He’s done a real good job defensively," Payton said of Morris. "They’re playing real good red-zone defense. They present a lot of problems.”
Vance Joseph vs. Kyle Shanahan
Joseph has nothing but respect for Shanahan, who he said is the best he's "coached against" at making second-half adjustments . The Broncos will have to account for tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey as passing targets, but last week's game against the Los Angeles Rams at least gave Joseph some exposure to such imperatives.
"Kyle is the best halftime adjustment coach I’ve ever coached against," Joseph said on Thursday.
With how well Shanahan has Brock Purdy playing right now, it could be a long day if Joseph and the Broncos' defense don't figure out how to get the 49ers off the field on third down. Purdy has yet to be sacked this season.
Nik Bonitto vs. Trent Williams
This matchup could be emblematic of how this game unfolds for the Broncos. If Bonitto is able to get some pressure on Purdy at Williams's expense, it could open up possibilities across the defense.
But if Williams shuts Bonitto down, it won't bode well for the Broncos' defensive outlook.

title: 49ers' Biggest Strengths—and the Weaknesses Broncos Can Exploit
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will be the best team the Denver Broncos have faced so far. That's saying something, considering the level of competition the Broncos have faced thus far.
The 49ers have an explosive offense and a defense that doesn't allow big plays, and they're quite good against the run and pass. However, the 49ers have played the Arizona Cardinals, Miami Dolphins, and a jet-lagged Los Angeles Rams team in Australia, so Denver will be the best team they've faced so far this season.
Both teams are working the tape to find the threats to prepare for and the biggest weaknesses to target. The 49ers are a great team, but I've identified the biggest threat they pose. I've also singled out their biggest vulnerability, just as the Broncos have.
McCaffrey is a threat in every phase, and the Broncos haven't fared well against running backs through three games. The Broncos will need a clear, concise plan if they want to prevent McCaffrey from taking over the game and making life extremely difficult for their defense.
Much of the pressure will fall on the Broncos' linebackers and safeties, which is a concern given how Alex Singleton and Brandon Jones have played. Even so, defensive coordinator Vance Joseph has to key in on McCaffrey to give his defense the best chance for success.
The 49ers don't really have an obvious weakness to attack on offense, but if I'm forced to call someone a weak link, it'd be McKivitz. He is actually having a good year so far, but he hasn't been overly challenged outside of the jet-lagged Rams defense.
This might be a game to use Nik Bonitto on the defensive left side of the line more frequently and match him up against McKivitz.
Jonah Elliss has a poor matchup against McKivitz, but Que Robinson is the one to watch. Robinson has outplayed Elliss so far this season, so it will be interesting to see whether the Broncos change the rotation at outside linebacker, given how these two have played.
Warner is one of the 49ers' few defensive weapons, and his game has few weaknesses. As with McCaffrey, Denver needs to find a way to handle Warner and keep him from taking over the game for the 49ers' defense.
The problem is that the 49ers have a good defense that can still thrive without Warner being a major factor. They're disciplined, and the defense isn't overly complicated, making it easier for players to do their jobs and play fast.
Let's hope the Broncos have a plan for Warner.
Odighizuwa is a fine player, but he is the 49ers' clear weak link on defense. He offers minimal pass-rush impact and looks like a liability against the run.
The 49ers' linebackers have largely covered Odighizuwa's issues, but Denver should be able to attack him in the run game for moderate success.
Left guard Ben Powers and right guard Quinn Meinerz should be able to handle Odighizuwa in both phases of the game. The 49ers don't have the best depth on their defensive line, so neutralizing Odighizuwa will go a long way toward limiting the unit's overall impact.

title: Final Injury Report: Several 49ers Starters in Jeopardy vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are getting a big boost entering their Week 4 road game against the San Francisco 49ers .
On Friday, the final injury report dropped, and while there is one piece of bad news on the Broncos' side of the fence, there's far more good, while the 49ers are dealing with a plethora of injuries. Several key 49ers have been ruled out, with the status of a few others being up in the air.
Let's take a look at where things stand entering Week 4 for both clubs, starting with the road team.
Being without Tillman might be tough, but the Broncos could elevate one of their practice squad outside linebackers. Based on what I've been told this week, if it happens, it'll be Johnny Walker.
The Broncos have Nik Bonitto, Jonah Elliss, and Que Robinson fully healthy. If Walker gets promoted, that'll keep their four-man edge rotation intact. But maybe they only dress three, and use that elevation on another position. We'll know on Saturday.
Mims is back, after missing the past two games with that foot injury. The Broncos tried to weather the storm of Mims's absence by first rolling with Kris Abrams-Draine as the punt returner, but he was nothing more than a reliable fair-catcher.
Last week, the Broncos elevated rookie returner Kolbe Katsis, and he provided a spark, finishing with a record debut as a returner . Many fans didn't love that he bobbled a couple of punt returns, though he didn't muff any.
The Broncos have their All-Pro returner back, and we'll see what the coaches have in store for Mims as a receiver. He can offer so much more than just his returner skills, as evidenced by how he led the Broncos in receiving in last year's playoff run.
Dobbins and Waddle are also good to go. Dobbins has been hobbled somewhat with that hip injury, but he's battled through it without missing any full games.
Waddle suffered a foot injury against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night, though it was quiet. We may not have known anything about it had he not been spotted leaving Empower Field at Mile High in a walking boot . Fortunately, though, he was a full participant in all three practices this week.
Allen and Jones each had one day of limited practice, but it was rest. Neither veteran is injured.
Here's the final injury report for #DENvsSF . The #49ers will be missing some key players, including Nick Bosa, while the #Broncos will only be without Dondrea Tillman. pic.twitter.com/eHvyjtaekx
As expected , Bosa has been ruled out, but so has Mykel Williams. That puts the 49ers down two edge rushers, including one Pro Bowler. Meanwhile, with White listed as questionable, if he suffers a setback between now and Sunday, that'll make it three edge defenders out.
We'll be keeping a close eye on Evans over the weekend. He's been off to a great start as a brand-new 49er. The veteran wideout quickly formed some good chemistry with quarterback Brock Purdy, so if Evans is a no-go game-time decision, it'll take some pressure off the Broncos' secondary.
It would be awesome to see Greenlaw suited up on Sunday, just for the storyline, but the former Broncos linebacker is up in the air. I expect that he'll play, but we won't find out until game day.
McCaffrey and Trent Williams received some rest days this week, although the All-World left tackle is dealing with a neck injury. Williams's matchup with Bonitto will be one of the keys to this game.

title: Why Broncos Cut Veteran WR to Promote Adam Prentice
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have promoted fullback Adam Prentice to the active roster ahead of their Week 4 road game against the San Francisco 49ers .
According to The Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson , Prentice is now on the 53-man roster. To make room for Prentice, the Broncos waived veteran wideout Lil'Jordan Humphrey.
The Broncos have become expert at playing the practice squad elevation game. The upside is that game-day elevations give the Broncos additional roster flexibility.
The downside is that, when a player maxes out his three-elevation limit, as Prentice did, the Broncos either have to promote him to the active roster or waive him. If he passes through waivers, he can then be re-signed to the practice squad where his three-elevation limit resets at zero.
I'm sure the Broncos plan on keeping Humphrey around on the practice squad, although, a team could come knocking. Humphrey is an experienced big-bodied receiver who actually can block and play special teams.
Because he's a vested veteran, Humphrey was released, not waived, which makes him free to sign with any team or to turn around and re-sign with the Broncos' practice squad. He was a healthy scratch last week against the Los Angeles Rams, but it's not as if Prentice played a lot.
The Broncos elevated Prentice for all three games thus far, and he played six, eight, and four snaps, respectively. However, the Broncos view him as being integral to the offense, and if they want to get this impotent run game off the ground, the fullback will be key.
It will require the Broncos to put Bo Nix under center far more than they have thus far, allowing Prentice to step in and lead block in the I or offset-I formation for the likes of J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. A big reason why Prentice hasn't been used that much, despite being elevated each week, is because of the flow of the game, where Denver has found itself trailing in the second half.
The Broncos have been forced to throw to get back into the past two games, which relegates the fullback to spectator status. But there were other opportunities to utilize him, just as they did in the preseason: on the goal-line late, Nix went up and over for a one-yard touchdown, stretching the ball out to break the plane, when the give could have just as easily gone to Prentice on a fullback dive.
Prentice hasn't let the Broncos down when he's been given the rock. Perhaps he'll start getting some higher usage as the season goes along.
At the very least, let's hope that Denver recommits to running the ball early in games, which would put Prentice on the field more as a lead blocker. He's one of the NFL's better fullbacks, and he's proven that he can do more than block.
Time will tell exactly what the Broncos have in store for Prentice, but the past week has seen the team's initial practice-squad machinations resolve with him and long snapper Mitchell Fraboni being promoted to the 53-man roster. Now, at least, it opens up the game-day elevation options to other potentially impact players, like returner Kolbe Katsis.
Heck, maybe we'll even see rookie linebacker Red Murdock at some point this season. You never know.
The Broncos announced on Saturday that Humphrey has been signed to the practice squad. He stays in the fold, as planned.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Victory Over the 49ers
full_text:
It hasn’t been the prettiest start for the Denver Broncos in 2026, but the fact is, they're 2-1.
That record came against three opponents expected to be playoff contenders this season.
Now comes another outing against an expected playoff contender — and in this game, the Broncos could be staring down an early Super Bowl favorite.
The San Francisco 49ers haven’t faced the toughest schedule to date , but they're doing what quality teams should be doing — that’s winning the games they are supposed to (and doing it decisively) and finding ways to beat quality teams.
The Los Angeles Rams may not have been prepared for the Week 1 showdown in Australia, but the 49ers executed on both sides of the ball. The 49ers dominated the Miami Dolphins, as one would expect a playoff contender to do against a rebuilding team, and they led 23-3 early in the third quarter against an Arizona Cardinals team that attempted an unsuccessful comeback.
This Week 4 matchup might be the toughest of the Broncos’ first six games , as it's on the road against a well-coached team that is playing at a high level. What will it take for Denver to prevail?
Let’s look at three keys to a Broncos victory over the 49ers and whether they can prove they are a threat to make a deep playoff run.
Bring up Purdy in a conversation, and few people assert him as an elite quarterback. The 2022 seventh-round pick (and Mr. Irrelevant that year) tends to be dismissed as a QB who only does well because of Kyle Shanahan’s system.
However, while Purdy does run Shanahan’s offense well, that doesn’t mean he’s a system quarterback. That’s especially true this season, as he’s off to what looks to be the best season of his five-year NFL career.
Purdy has nine touchdown passes in three games. If he keeps up that pace, he’ll finish with 51 touchdown passes, which would be an impressive number and one that would make him a legitimate choice for NFL MVP.
Purdy may not get respect from some because he isn’t a flashy passer, but he’s a smart player who understands the importance of making quick decisions. It does help that he has a lot of playmakers around him on offense, but he deserves credit for what he has done to improve as a QB.
It’s worth noting that Purdy has not been sacked this season. The Broncos' pass rush will be looking to end that run, but they will have to contend with a good offensive line and Purdy’s ability to get rid of the ball quickly.
If the Broncos want a chance to win this game, they must contain Purdy and not assume that he’s just a system QB.
While Purdy deserves all the credit in the world for his play, he is surrounded by a lot of talented playmakers on offense. Some of these playmakers are 30 years or older, but they've all shown they have plenty left in the tank.
Mike Evans joined the 49ers in free agency this past offseason, and he is still productive, with 12 receptions for 137 yards and two touchdowns thus far. Evans is dealing with a rib injury , though there’s a chance he’ll play on Sunday.
But even if Evans is out, the Broncos still have to contend with two notable names: Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle. McCaffrey is averaging 4.7 yards per carry through three games, with three rushing touchdowns. He also has 13 receptions, making him a threat as both a runner and a pass catcher.
Kittle already has three touchdowns this season, and the Broncos have had issues containing tight ends over the past couple of years. But they will have to find a way to limit Kittle’s impact, regardless of who they task with defending him.
The 49ers have a good No. 2 running back in Kaelon Black, who is averaging 4.3 yards per carry, and Deebo Samuel continues to show he can be a threat as a runner, receiver, and return man.
After the issues the Broncos had on pass defense against the Rams — in which neither Patrick Surtain II nor Riley Moss had their best game — the onus will be on the defensive backfield to show it can bounce back. But it will be against a number of quality playmakers.
Although the Broncos are 2-1 to start the season, they've been fortunate that their inability to move the ball and score points in the first half hasn’t cost them in the last two games. The Broncos have scored just 10 first-half points and were shut out in the first half against the Rams last week.
Asking the Broncos' defense to continue to do the heavy lifting in the first half isn’t a recipe for success, especially when it comes against a top NFL offense like the 49ers'. While some first-half issues can be attributed to good defensive play by opponents, much of the blame belongs to the Broncos' offense and the players simply not executing.
Over three weeks, the 49ers have held opponents to 3.7 yards rushing per carry and 5.7 yards per pass play. While the 49ers are expected to be without edge rusher Nick Bosa this week, they have some capable players on defense, notably linebacker Fred Warner, who excels at getting to the ball and limiting offensive playmakers. Warner leads the Niners in tackles with 33 this season.
The Broncos offensive line, which was arguably the unit's biggest strength last year, hasn’t gotten off to a good start. In order for the Broncos to have a chance to finish more drives in the first half, the offensive line must be in sync to start, thus taking some pressure off Bo Nix, who needs to be more decisive and stop trying to force things that aren't there.
While the Cardinals scored 24 points in the second half of the Week 3 matchup with the 49ers, they were down 17-6 at halftime, and San Francisco scored on the opening drive of the second half. If the Broncos can’t manage at least 10 points in the first half, it will be harder to come back, particularly if the 49ers' offense gets off to a good start.
The Rams game was a big test that the Broncos passed, though they didn’t make it easy on themselves. But the 49ers are arguably a bigger test, given that it's a road game and the strong start this opponent has had.
Between a quarterback playing at an MVP level, plenty of offensive playmakers, and a defense that may not be dominant but can still give a team fits, the Broncos have their work cut out for them. How they perform this week will say a lot about where this team is ultimately headed.
If the Broncos have a good first half on both sides of the ball and keep this one close, win or lose, it'll be a sign they could be a top threat. But another slow start is more likely than not to mean a 2-2 record and plenty of questions to be answered going into Week 5.

title: Mile High Roundtable: Our Broncos-49ers Predictions
full_text:
For the first time since Sean Payton became the head coach, the Denver Broncos have opened the season 2-1.
It hasn't been easy, but the Broncos have overcome some concerning offensive foibles and a less-than-dominant defense to knock off two high-quality opponents back-to-back. Those two wins were at home, though, and the Broncos now take to the road for a Week 4 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers .
The 49ers are undefeated, riding high on Brock Purdy and their explosive offense. Across the board, the 49ers rank top 10 in all the key offensive categories.
The Broncos will have their work cut out for them, especially on the road. But there's something special about the belief this team has in itself; no deficit is insurmountable and anything is possible.
How will this one shake out? Let's go around the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle table to see how our staff foresees Broncos-49ers unfolding.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 2-1 : Late-game moxie from Bo Nix is one thing, but going on the road and taking down an undefeated Super Bowl contender is quite another. Surely another slow start would likely handicap the Broncos, so Davis Webb must find some offensive balance early. Even so, Nix has that John Elway knack for having ice water in his veins and ultimately leads the Broncos to another late win amid a three-touchdown performance.
Pick : Broncos 38, 49ers 31
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 2-1 : Through three weeks, there might not be another team looking better than the 49ers. They're banged up , though, giving the Broncos a great opportunity to get another statement win. The Broncos must shut down either George Kittle or Christian McCaffrey if they hope to win this game. The Broncos get it done, loading up the box to stop the run and making Purdy uncomfortable for the first time all season long. J.K. Dobbins has his best game of the year so far, and the Broncos get a nice road win.
Pick : Broncos 27, 49ers 20
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 2-1 : On paper, the Broncos simply don't measure up to the 49ers. Statistically, these two teams are far apart, and yet, when it matters most, the Broncos collectively play their best ball, making them a threat against any team, including the cream of the NFL crop. I shudder to think how the Broncos would lay waste to opponents if they could get 60 minutes of production out of their offense, but a boy can only dream. Like Carl, I see this game being Dobbins's coming-out party, reminding everyone that he's still the man in Denver's backfield. Meanwhile, Jaylen Waddle returns to the 100-yard club and Nik Bonitto gets the better of Trent Williams in another Broncos stunner.
Pick : Broncos 33, 49ers 30
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 2-1 : This, more than any game on the schedule as we currently know it, scares me the most. And it’s not often I pick against the Broncos, but I’m still apprehensive about this team playing all 60 minutes rather than just showing up after halftime. It’s gonna be ugly if that happens again — a repeat of Week 1. I ultimately expect Denver to battle hard, and they’re never out of a game with Nix, but this road matchup against a white-hot 49ers squad could simply prove to be insurmountable. Reverse jinx time.
Pick : 49ers 29, Broncos 22
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 2-1 : The 49ers have arguably the best offense in the NFL, and Purdy is off to his best start as a pro. The Broncos cannot afford a slow start because they can't count on the 49ers beating themselves the way the Los Angeles Rams did. Between Purdy's play and the playmakers on offense, the Broncos' defense has a tough task ahead, and the offense will need to produce early. Until I see that offense have a strong first half, though, it's hard to see the Broncos getting the win against a team that has been strong through the first three weeks.
Pick : 49ers 27, Broncos 17
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 1-2 : Another week against a QB playing at an MVP level, it’s still fair to say we don’t know who these 49ers are with a weird-circumstance game down under vs. the Rams and two wins versus teams thought of as stinkers in the Arizona Cardinals and Miami Dolphins. Still, Kyle Shanahan schemes up the run game and pass game to isolate linebackers as good as anyone in the league, and the 49ers look as good as anyone. Not a week to play possum in the first half as Denver has done this season.
Pick : 49ers 24, Broncos 23
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 1-2 : Denver desperately needs offensive consistency to beat the 49ers this week, and taking bite-sized pieces in a ball control offense is going to be key. If they can't stay ahead of the chains and are forced to punt a lot, it could get ugly quickly. San Francisco's offense is the league's most polished unit, and they can score at will. Everything in my brain tells me to take the 49ers at home, but my gut says that the "Heart Attack Horses" find a way to win it.
Pick : Broncos 24, 49ers 23
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 1-2 : The 49ers have been one of the best teams ever through three weeks, but their schedule hasn't been the onslaught Denver has faced. Both have beaten the Rams, but San Fran got L.A. on a bad travel schedule to Australia, which made things easier due to jet lag. Denver has been tested in ways the 49ers haven't, and it hasn't been the prettiest. But Denver is 2-1. Both teams are each other's toughest matchup so far this season, but the 49ers' injury situation leads to their first loss as Denver once again pulls one out late.
Pick : Broncos 31, 49ers 23
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 1-2 : The 49ers have had one of the best offenses in the NFL over the first three weeks with Purdy, Kittle, and McCaffrey leading the charge. Injuries still plague them, however, with the biggest question marks being defensive end Nick Bosa and Pro Bowl wideout Mike Evans. Despite my worries about the Broncos' linebackers versus Kittle and McCaffrey and the fact that Purdy has yet to be sacked, the Broncos pull out another win on their way to sweeping the NFC West.
Pick : Broncos 24, 49ers 20
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 0-3 : The 49ers have shown they're a top team with a dangerous offense. The combination of McCaffrey and Kittle could mean a long day for Denver's beleaguered linebacker unit. In this one, the Broncos offense has its moments and makes it interesting late, with Dobbins having a vintage performance and Nix looking more consistently composed. However, even with injuries, the 49ers figure to have a little too much for the Broncos.
Pick : 49ers 31, Broncos 21

title: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Carolina Panthers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will try to notch back-to-back wins for the first time in 2026 when they square off with the injury-depleted Carolina Panthers Sunday night.
The Lions are coming off a 31-24 triumph over Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets in Week 3. Meanwhile, the Panthers will try to bounce back from a 21-18 loss to Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns.
Here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 4 matchup with Carolina.
Sunday marks another opportunity for the Lions to show off their ability in front of a national audience. In their first primetime showing this year, the Lions weren't able to match the Bills' hot start and as a result suffered a difficult loss. However, this time they have a distinct upper hand with how banged up the Panthers are at this point.
Carolina has placed three significant members of their roster on injured reserve this week alone, including both of their starting cornerbacks. As a result, the Lions' offense should be able to grill the Carolina defense.
However, the Lions' secondary has had its own issues, which leads me to believe this game could get close to being a shootout. I think Detroit has enough to win, but Bryce Young is playing at a high level and won't go down without a fight. The Lions move to 3-1, thanks to some clutch plays down the stretch.
The Detroit Lions will square off with an injury-depleted Carolina Panthers squad Sunday night.
For starters, Carolina will be without both of its starting outside cornerbacks, Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin), for the Week 4 contest. Subsequently, Jared Goff & Co. should have a sizable advantage in their matchup with the Panthers’ pass defense.
Plus, Carolina will be without multiple offensive linemen: Guard Damien Lewis (UCL) and offensive tackles Ikem Ekwonu (patella tendon) and Taylor Moton (blood clot in lung).
The Lions, to me, should have the upper hand in this primetime affair due to the sheer number of injuries on the Panthers’ roster.
As a result, I believe Dan Campbell's squad leaves Charlotte with the Week 4 victory.
It is hard not to imagine Jahmyr Gibbs getting a hefty workload this week. Carolina has the worst rush defense in the league, giving up north of five yards per carry.
Detroit's offense has had a consistent start to the season, scoring 31 points in each of their first three games.
If Detroit's offense can get off to a quicker start, it may be difficult for the Panthers to keep up all evening.
The biggest area of concern for Detroit's defense this week is guarding tight ends. If the struggles continue, the game may be closer than expected.
The Lions enter their second primetime game of the year as slight favorites despite being the road team. The offense has proven solid for Detroit so far, putting up 31 points every game. Defense, however, is suspect, as Motown allows their opponents back into the game at every chance.
That makes Sunday’s matchup intriguing. Jared Goff is closer to Caleb Williams when it comes to talent when compared to Deshaun Watson, so a 31-point game is likely on the way. The question becomes if the Lions defense shows up.
I will say Aidan Hutchinson gets a clutch sack to keep the Lions afloat.

title: Lions WR Hit With Hefty Fine After Jets Game
full_text:
Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams received a fine from the NFL for the second straight week.
Williams was hit with a $23,417 fine for unnecessary roughness, stemming from his use of his helmet on a play in the third quarter of the team's Week 3 win. The fifth-year wideout was the only Lions player to receive a fine in the game against the Jets.
The Alabama product was not penalized during the game for the hit. A replay indicates that Williams appears to lower his head while bracing for impact from a Jets defender after making a reception.
Last week, Williams was one of six players fined for incidents in Detroit's Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He accrued two separate fines, one for $14,926 regarding illegal celebrations and vulguar acts and another for taunting worth $11,941.
Detroit has had at least one player fined in each of its first three games. In Week 1, running back Jahmyr Gibbs was hit with a fine for use of the helmet on a run against the New Orleans Saints.
Through three games, Williams has recorded 10 catches for 127 yards. His trademark explosiveness and game-breaking speed have been limited by opposing defenses utilizing two deep safeties to prevent him from stretching the field.
Additional Lions Insider Analysis: Players Who Need Bounceback Game Against Panthers
The wideout is a former first-round pick by the Lions, who traded up in the 2022 NFL Draft to select him 12th overall. After a torn ACL suffered in his final collegiate game cost him the start of his rookie year, Williams had his first career catch go for a 41-yard touchdown late in that season.
Since then, Williams has gradually improved overall and is now coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. Up to this point in his career, Williams has notched 158 receptions for 2,640 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Though an argument can be made that he has struggled from a statistical perspective, his gravity as a receiver has opened up opportunities for others within the offense. His counterpart Amon-Ra St. Brown has recorded 23 catches for 228 yards and five touchdowns through the season's first three games.

title: Detroit Lions Elevate Safety From Practice Squad Against Panthers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have officially revealed their Week 4 practice squad elevation, ahead of a primetime Sunday Night Football road contest against the Carolina Panthers.
According to the team, safety Jalen Mills has been elevated from the practice squad for the second straight week.
Only guard Ben Bartch was ruled out prior to the game, while veteran D.J. Reed is questionable for the game after battling a rib injury all week. He was limited at practice this week, but there is no indication he will miss the contest against the NFC South opponent.
For new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, he has not yet started to plan how the offense will handle when center Cade Mays returns to the lineup after his wrist injury heals.
“Yeah, right now honestly, not there mentally," said Petzing. "I think as that comes to fruition, it's one of those things like deal with the problem when it presents itself. It'd be a great problem to have, and our goal is always going to be to figure out how to get our best five on the field.”
One of the primary goals for the Lions' defense will be to contain Panthers quarterback Bryce Young. Surprisingly, he has only three recorded rushing attempts in the first three weeks of the 2026 regular season.
Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week if he was surprised at that low total.
“I am. I am because that's been something that he's done quite a bit of and really hurts defenses," Campbell said. "So I am, but no matter what it is, his eyes are always downfield. And then it's okay, well it's not there. I'm out in the open. I'll take off. So, he's still dangerous. It still shows up. I mean, he had one in Chicago Week 1 that was -- there it is, man. You just gave him the lane.
"Everybody's covered up and then he takes it all the way. So I am, but that whole thing doesn't mean anything because I'm like, we better be ready. I mean, he could take off 10 times this game for all I know if we give it to him.”

title: 3 Lions Players That Need Bounceback Game Against Panthers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions enter their Week 4 contest with the Panthers looking to notch a second consecutive win.
While the Lions feature plenty of talent on both sides of the ball, three defensive players, in particular, need to deliver much stronger performances Sunday night.
Each of the players below have underwhelmed thus far this season, and are candidates to bounce back in Detroit's primetime affair in Carolina.
Campbell has had a nightmarish start to the 2026 campaign. And he hasn't come anywhere close to replicating his Pro Bowl-caliber production from a season ago.
In fact, through three games, he's earned just a 44.2 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, ranking a measly 61st among 67 qualified linebackers. And he's especially struggled in coverage, allowing a passer rating of 149.4 on passes thrown his way.
Quite simply, Campbell has underachieved thus far this season, and needs to perform at a much higher level in order for the Lions’ defense to reach its full potential.
He has a tough task ahead of himself Sunday night facing Bryce Young and the Panthers’ fifth-ranked offense . However, if he can find a way to get back on track, it'd go a long way toward Detroit securing the Week 4 victory.
Reed will take on a banged-up Panthers receiving corps Sunday.
Xavier Legette, Carolina's No. 3 receiver, has already been ruled out for the Week 4 contest. Meanwhile, Jalen Coker, the team's leading receiver with 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns, is presently questionable with a quad injury.
If Coker is ruled out, Panthers wideout Tetairoa McMillan will undoubtedly become the main focus of Reed and the Lions’ secondary.
Through three weeks, Reed has been underwhelming in coverage. He's allowed a passer rating of 131.9 on passes thrown his way – 85th out of 97 qualified cornerbacks – and 20.3 yards per reception (92nd among qualified CBs).
Along with all that, he's already allowed 10 receptions on balls thrown his way. Plus, he's recorded zero interceptions and just one pass defensed. And for his efforts, he's earned a 60.5 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, ranking 45th among qualified corners.
Detroit's secondary direly needs him to perform more like a No. 1 CB in the weeks ahead, including on Sunday night in Carolina.
Rodriguez hasn't made much of an impact through the season's first three weeks . He's logged just 54 overall snaps and seven total tackles, but could play himself into a bigger role with a solid showing against Carolina.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit could use much more from Rodriguez and the Lions’ entire linebackers unit in Week 4 and beyond. Providing Rodriguez with increased responsibilities could be an important step in that process.

title: 2 Lions Players Who Could Have Expanded Roles Against Panthers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are hoping their young players continue to develop and make plays out on the football field.
Two players that have started to catch the attention of the coaching staff are tight end Jackson Meeks and linebacker Jimmy Rolder.
Both have been used on special teams, but could see their roles expanded this week, against the Carolina Panthers or in the very near future.
Meeks is a converted wide receiver and has been steadily learning the tight end position.
“Yeah, Meeks, he gives us everything he's got every week, practice squad and then the reps we do give him. If we get Sam (LaPorta) out for a rep or Brock (Wright), we give him some reps. And there again, he's just growing, man. He's still so raw to the position, but yet he's growing and it means something to him and he works at it and he's a pretty smart guy for a young guy," said Dan Campbell. "And for somebody that hadn't played the position, he's pretty aware . So it's time on task, but we like where he's going. And a lot of that right now is special teams.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: How to Watch, Listen, Stream Week 4 Contest Against Panthers
"That's the biggest part of where he's at and why he's at the game is because he really helps us on special teams. But the faster he can grow, the more we'll use him," Campbell added further. "And Rolder's the same thing. We got one sample size of him and that looked good on special teams. Is that here to stay? Do you continue to get better? We'd like to mix him in at times if we could this game on some defense, but we'll see where that's at.”
Detroit's defense has struggled mightily to start the 2026 NFL season, especially in coverage. The coaching staff even made the decision to bench veteran Devin White against the New York Jets.
Rolder had a productive first training camp, including recording a couple of interceptions. He could find himself moving up the depth chart, if he is able to take advantage of his opportunities.

title: 5 Players Lions Must Scout: One That Will Make Fans Forget Joey Porter Jr.
full_text:
The Detroit Lions sit at 2-1 as they head on a crucial road trip to Carolina to take on the Panthers on Sunday Night Football. Before they can dive into the Week 4 action, however, the college football world is in action for Week 5.
The Lions will be looking to gain key contributors in their 2027 draft, as the early returns on the 2026 class are mixed and a lackluster 2024 class looms large.
Here are five players the Detroit Lions must scout who could build their core in Week 5.
Cole sits as one of the top linebackers in the 2027 class. His athleticism is one of his key strengths, and that makes him a nightmare to opposing teams when blitzing. The Bulldogs defender already sits at 1.5 sacks through four games, with the Bulldogs the No. 2 team in the country.
His play recognition needs some work, but his athleticism makes him an intriguing pick and potentially another early-round linebacker after CJ Allen went to Indianapolis in the second round this past April.
Cole’s Bulldogs host the Vanderbilt Commodores at 12:45 p.m. EST on Saturday.
It is a two Bulldog week on the draft board, as Bolden is another player that the Lions need to turn on the tape for. The safety is versatile, but is projected as a free safety at the pro level.
He is a solid tackler, but needs to bulk up to physically compete one-on-one with receivers. However, with the lack of a solid Kerby Joseph timeline in Motown, Bolden can be a top pick that will make an impact on the field. It either frees up Brian Branch to play the nickel spot, or Bolden could slot in as Joseph’s replacement. Regardless, it would be a homerun pick.
The eyes stay on the SEC this week, as Alabama squares off with “Super Kamario” Taylor and the Mississippi State Bulldogs. Brown will be tasked with holding Taylor’s arm in check by locking down one side of the field.
Brown, at 6-foot, has the size desired for a corner, and can play on the outside level. He has sticky man coverage, which is a must to be in the Lions secondary, although he did allow too many yards in coverage last season. He has the straight line speed to make up for it at this level, too, but that is not the case in the pros.
The Lions’ issue at the cornerback position is well-documented, and Brown is an instant impact player. This game against Taylor’s Bulldogs could be huge for the 20-year-old, as a strong game bumps him from early-second round consideration into Day 1 conversations.
The Crimson Tide travel to Mississippi State at noon EST.
Shuler is a rare blend of a safety that can roam the field and be a threat alongside being unafraid to knock a player out of their cleats. He lines up everywhere for the Irish, and is well-respected in the locker room, being voted a team captain.
The safety has the instincts in coverage and the versatility needed to be a real contributor at the NFL level. Shuler has the hit power to be a force in the league, with Michigan State head coach Pat Fitzgerald quipping that he “knocked a kid’s lips off” against Rice.
However, his hit power does come with a very high missed tackle count, which must be cleaned up in order for Shuler to be an impact player and move into Day Two conversations for the 2027 NFL Draft.
Shuler’s Irish travel to North Carolina to play the Tar Heels at noon EST.
The FCS has had talented and athletic quarterbacks earn looks in the last few years. North Dakota State sent Cam Miller and Cole Payton into the NFL as Day 3 picks in the last two seasons, and Brungard may be taking the mantle this season.
The versatile dual-threat quarterback has a ridiculous highlight tape, and this season looks to be just as good. The Ohio native has completed over 74 percent of his passes for 1,216 yards this season, and has added 461 yards and seven more house calls on the ground.
Defenses simply cannot account for Brungard’s strengths. In 2025, Brungard had 54 total touchdowns, split down the middle with 26 through the air and 27 on the ground. That accounts for 53 of his touchdowns, as his other was a 50-yard receiving touchdown, of course.
When looking for a potential change-of-pace or red-zone wrinkle for Drew Petzing’s offense, Brungard is that player. Dan Campbell knows about the dangers of a Taysom Hill package from his time in New Orleans, and Brungard could be the late round or undrafted option.
The Penguins’ star player is also well experienced, being in his third season as a collegiate starter with YSU.
Youngstown State travels to Southern Illinois at 5 p.m. EST.

title: How To Watch, Listen, Stream Detroit Lions Against Carolina Panthers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are seeking their third victory of the 2026 season and first away from Ford Field.
Carolina is entering the Week 4 Sunday Night Football contest banged up, but Dan Campbell still knows the challenges of facing off against an opponent that qualified for the playoffs last season.
"It'll be loud. It's going to be one of those environments that we've got to be able to have poise under those circumstances. They're coming off of a loss, and so they're going to want to make that right. At home, big game for them," said Campbell earlier this week. "So, we’ll get their best shot. I think (Panthers head coach Dave) Canales has done a heck of a job over there. They won that division last year, playoff team. They've got plenty of weapons. Defensive scheme has been there now going on really, I guess four years now.
"It's a sound, aggressive unit. They play headsy, they play where their help's at. It's fed by really this front seven, front six, that D-line led by (Defensive tackle Derrick) Brown and (Outside linebacker Jaelan) Phillips. And then I think they'll get (Linebacker Devin) Lloyd back this week. So, he's pretty dang versatile, does a lot for them. And then special teams, they give you a lot of different looks. They can be problematic."

Detroit's defense will again be tasked with limiting a mobile quarterback.
"We’ve just got to stay true to what we are, what we know, discipline. We've got to improve a little bit here this week. Every week you've got to improve, but this is a good opponent. Their offense over there, Bryce (Young) makes it problematic," said Campbell. "He's got a quick release. He sees it. They're doing a good job there. They're under center, they're in pistol, they're in gun, boots, keepers, RPOs, dot runs. (Running back Chuba) Hubbard runs hard, and then they've got targets now .
"They've got big skill between these receivers and the tight ends. These are big, tall possession guys that can go above the rim and are strong at the catchpoint. So, this will be a good test. But we're looking forward to it coming off of the win against the Jets here. And so next one up.”

title: Detroit Lions Ownership Looks Legendary Compared to Corny Chris Ilitch
full_text:
It was uncomfortable. Very uncomfortable.
Sitting in the press box at Ford Field, this writer observed fans of the Detroit Lions deciding it was time to send a message to ownership.
For years, the team was simply known for incompetence, disrespecting players, losing seasons and being among the very small number of teams that had a season with no victories.
It was that September 26, 2021 halftime speech at Ford Field from owner Sheila Hamp, intended to honor wide receiver Calvin Johnson and his entry into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, that fans sent a clear message. Stop being a loser and stop asking for money back from players when they retire.
It was awkward, uncomfortable but much needed. The response from ownership was to be even more transparent, actually speaking to the media when team issues popped up. When Dan Campbell started his second season with a 1-6 record, Hamp addressed the rumblings publicly and gave Campbell and general manager Brad Holmes a vote of confidence.
Since 2022, the Lions have enjoyed four consecutive winning seasons and are a team that should be in the playoffs consistently.
Interestingly, the Lions still like asking for money back from players. Business is business, I guess.
Red Wings and Detroit Tigers owner, Chris Ilitch, is now facing the same wrath from fans.
At the Red Wings season-opener, fans began chanting "Sell the Team, Sell the Team" just five minutes into the game against the New York Rangers.
Oh! It is going to be a LONG season @AdamRStroz https://t.co/Wj6VBmFM7H
During introductions, former team captain Dylan Larkin was booed by the home crowd.
This is what it has come to for the Red Wings. A disastrous 10-year period marked by a lack of success, stamped with a home-grown talent demanding to be traded.
“Dylan today being part of the team, he wanted to be out there for the ceremony. So, let me make that real clear,” coach Todd McLellan said. “That’s what our team has done for 101 years now, is put the players out there. And Dylan’s explanation was, I don’t want the rest of my teammates, the ones that aren’t dressed, to not be out there.
“So, we went out as a team, and that’s what we’re going to do. Obviously he’s got to live with the ramifications of asking for a trade. It’s not comfortable for anybody. I feel bad for him. I do.”
The decision to send Larkin out there to be embarrassed was lampooned by TNT broadcasters, calling it "bush league."
Could it impact free agents wanting to come to Detroit to play hockey? Probably not. Ilitch is described as a fiscally responsible owner, otherwise known as cheap .
It is not like NHL free agents are demanding their agents land them in Motown.
Ilitch decided the best way to address the ills of the Red Wings was to answer written questions from a columnist known for witty television antics far more than his hard-hitting opinions on Detroit sports matters.
The lack of public accountability has forced fans to now share their frustrations publicly at Little Caesars Arena.
Hamp and the Lions tackled it head on. Ilitch ran and hid behind a "friendly" media member.
Not answering questions and not sharing the plan for the Red Wings is one way to approach it. But, the consequences are going to be felt. More embarrassing nights are ahead for an organization that replaced Steve Yzerman with an interim general manager.
This writer was a little surprised that many qualified front office executives did not want this opportunity. But the Red Wings do not have the same mystique and aura any longer.
The "Yzerplan" failed and their owner is scared of accountability .

title: Amon-Ra St. Brown: Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs Is 'Just a Freak'
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will be squaring off with a Carolina Panthers team devoid of its top two cornerback on Sunday. Both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson suffered injuries in Week 3 that will cause them to sit out Sunday and the following three weeks as a result of being placed on Carolina's injured reserve list .
It leaves the Panthers having to rely on a pair of second-stringers to contain the Lions’ pass-catching duo of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. While that is expected to be a tough task for Carolina’s reserve corners, St. Brown and Williams could also be challenged going up against a new-look secondary without an ample amount of time for preparation.
"Obviously, you don't know how they feel about their backup corners,” St. Brown told reporters Thursday. “If they feel good, they'll probably continue to do the same, similar stuff. If not, maybe they'll mix some things up.
“But, I feel like we've been getting a lot of different looks from what we've seen on tape with a lot of the opponents that we've played this year. So, we're expecting one thing, but also you can expect the unexpected, too. So, we've got to be able to make adjustments in the game and things like that. But, I think the thing that goes with any game really, you got to make adjustments throughout the game.”
St. Brown is not coming off one of his stronger performances, either. In fact, a week ago against the Jets, he secured just four catches for 19 yards and a touchdown – by far, his lowest statistical output of the 2026 campaign.
With St. Brown's production curtailed, the Lions needed somebody to step up, and it happened to be their do-it-all lead back, Jahmyr Gibbs.
Gibbs delivered a standout performance in the Week 3 affair , recording 99 yards and a couple of touchdowns on the ground plus another 65 yards and a score as a pass-catcher.
Petzing & Co. have not been afraid to deploy Gibbs as a receiver this season, a sign of how valuable the fourth-year back is to the team's offense.
And per St. Brown, Gibbs has put in the time to hone his route-running and all-around receiving ability.
“Jahmyr is naturally gifted in certain areas. So, a lot of stuff that you'd have to tell certain guys, you don't have to tell him,” St. Brown said of the talented runner. “But, there's still an element of receiver he's never really played. It's like if you put me at running back, there's things I don't know. And he understands what he knows and doesn't know, and he'll ask me all those questions and he's a quick learner. You love to have that as a coach and being his teammate, it's easy to tell him to do this and he does it the next time. So, he's just a freak, man.”
With the injuries to the Panthers’ defensive backs room, it wouldn't be surprising to see the Lions have a big night offensively on Sunday. Drew Petzings's unit has performed at a high level so far this season, too, averaging 31 points a game through the first three weeks.
Yet, St. Brown is convinced the offense is still capable of more.
“I feel like we can still be a lot better as an offense,” the sixth-year receiver said. “We have so much more to improve on, which is awesome because we have put up a good amount of points the first three weeks. But, I feel like we can, we still have so much to get better at.
“Drew's done a great job obviously. We're all still learning things. We're all trying to get better each and every week, especially at this point in the season, you've got some games under your belt. You've got some tape to watch from other teams. So, it's going to be exciting these next few weeks.”

title: Detroit Lions Rule Out OL Against Carolina Panthers, CB Questionable
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official Week 4 injury designation report.
Offensive guard Ben Bartch, who missed all week of practice dealing with a foot injury, has been ruled out of the Week 4 Sunday Night Football contest against the Carolina Panthers.
Cornerback D.J. Reed, who has been listed as limited with a rib injury, is not expected to be held out of action.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard called it an honor to coach the veteran defensive back earlier this week.
The 29-year-old has not had the best start to the season and had his difficulties with New York Jets receiver Garrett Wilson in the fourth-quarter last week.
“Yeah. It's an honor to coach a player like D.J. because he's totally accountable, totally accountable," said Sheppard. "He's kind of like Jack (Campbell) in that sense to where he doesn't like, 'Oh, what are you talking to me about that?' He's right now, 'Coach, I got to be better.' Well, how? When I'm in that scenario, I'm on the red line. You should do this. When I'm off the red line, do that. He has these answers because he's got a lot of time on task in this league. And to be quite frank with you, D.J.'s in phase on a lot of these balls and he understands that."
Reed, despite making plays throughout the Jets game, lamented some tough catches that Wilson was able to make, since it allowed the Jets to make comeback in the fourth quarter.
"I told him, 'What is the standard, being in phase or making the play at the point of attack?' He answered, 'Coach, I got to make those plays and I will.' And I'll be honest with you, the one catch that Garrett Wilson had, I believe it might have been 4th-and-6. Listen, I mean, my gosh, that's why that guy's paid 30 million a year," said Sheppard. "He's through the basket, back down through the basket. The ball's coming out and he re-catches it. When that stuff happens, all good, D.J., let's go. Next play.
"It's more important trying to get him to the next play. And listen, stuff happens. 'That ain't good enough, Shepp.' And he's mad at himself trying to get him to the next play and understanding, 'I like where you're at on that coverage. We'll find a way to get it out.' But in some of these scenarios, D.J.'s totally in phase. It's about finishing at the point of attack.”

title: Desperate Times: Three Reasons Why Packers Will Lose to Buccaneers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Coming off last week’s embarrassing loss to the Falcons, the Green Bay Packers desperately need a win on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
In a sign that desperate times lead to desperate measures, the Packers signed veteran guards Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler this week to cover up for their enormous mistakes in building their offensive line.
How will that group handle the pressure brought by the winless Buccaneers, who might be even more desperate than the Packers?
Perhaps not well, which is a reason why they will suffer a crushing loss in sweltering Tampa Bay.
As the saying goes, it’s not the heat, it’s the humidity. The kickoff forecast is obscene. At 1 p.m. Eastern, it’s supposed to be 89 degrees with a real-feel of 104 because of the humidity, according to AccuWeather . There’s a 50 percent chance of rain during the second half, with the temperature inching past 90.
The Packers don’t have much experience with these hellish conditions. Dating to the start of the Brett Favre era, the Packers have played only four road games with a kickoff temperature of 88 or hotter. That includes two games during the Matt LaFleur era. The Packers beat the Buccaneers 14-12 in 2022 and lost to the Buccaneers 38-10 in 2020.
All-time, the Packers are 3-8 at Raymond James Stadium. They are 1-3 when it’s hotter than 80 at kickoff.
“It’s a switch up, man, especially from being up here,” slot defender Javon Bullard said. “But I train in Florida, Georgia, Texas, so I’m always down South. It’s a challenge. It’s definitely a challenge because you talk about when your wind goes out, that’s when a lot of technique goes out. That’s when your brain stops to function, for real.
“Honestly, you try to catch your breath, you missing out on opportunities. So, I think that’s a challenge for us but we got to embrace it.”
The weather will pose a big challenge for the Packers, who might be relying on new guards Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler, neither of whom had a training camp so might not be in peak physical condition, and will be shorthanded at defensive tackle without Warren Brinson and Anthony Campbell.
The Packers need a win today. And they'll get it. Here are three reasons why the Packers will beat the Buccaneers (with the other side of this story coming up shortly). ⬇️ https://t.co/3KwFYpDnCd
For an added bonus, air quality will be poor.
Last week against the best run defense in the NFL, the Packers basically admitted defeat before the game began.
Facing Atlanta’s stout defense, the Packers gave the ball to their running backs eight times. In the first quarter, which ended with a 7-7 score, the play-calling consisted of 12 passes and three runs. In the second quarter, when the Packers had two possessions when the score was 7-7 or 10-7, it was seven passes and two runs.
Immediately after the game and throughout the week, coach Matt LaFleur spoke of the need to run the ball more.
“I think that’s one of the things whether you’re a running back, quarterback, D-lineman, you’ve got to allow guys to get into a rhythm,” he said. “And, certainly, if you run the ball nine times, it’s hard for them to do that. …
“Not every run has to be an explosive gain. Sometimes, you’ve just got to go hit it and get 3 yards, and it’s 3 yards and a cloud of dust just to stay on schedule and set yourself up for some more manageable third downs.”
Judging by his comments throughout the week, it seems clear the Packers are going to want to come out of the gates trying to establish their running game. But will they have any success?
Atlanta is first in the NFL with 47.7 rushing yards allowed per game and 2.75 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay is second with 76.0 rushing yards allowed per game and 3.12 yards allowed per carry.
At this point, the Packers might celebrate finishing a game with 76.0 rushing yards. They’ve rushed for 66, 63 and 17 yards in the three games with a league-worst 3.02-yard average. It’s early, obviously, but they are on pace to field the worst rushing attack in NFL history.
“They’re really good against the run. Really physical front. They play with a lot of guys in the box,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said of the Bucs.
The run defense starts with defensive tackle Vita Vea, who is listed at 6-foot-4 and 347 pounds. Will the Packers be able to move him in order to improve upon their 31st-ranked 3.0-yard rushing average on first down?
“You don’t have that many humans that big that can move and throw people around like that,” new right guard Kevin Zeitler said. “There’s the giant monsters in the league and he has his own special place there.”
LaFleur said the Bucs’ run defense starts with Vea.
“He’s a big human, but it’s not just him,” he said. “They do a great job with their edge setters, and the linebackers are physical. The secondary will punish you, as well. So, I think collectively, just all 11 do a really good job.”
The Packers are running the ball just 26.6 percent of the time – by far the lowest rate in the league (the Steelers are at 33.8 percent). That’s just not the basis of LaFleur’s offense; they were fifth in 2025 and third in 2024.
Because of a running game that’s been equal parts forgotten and ineffective, the Packers on third down have thrown 35 passes vs. only one run. Talks about one-sided and predictable.
“We always talk about having a complementary offense,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “Being able to lean on the run game is going to take some of the pressure off some of the pass protection and not let the D-line know we’re in pass situations. It’s something that we’ve got to improve. We can’t have a game where we have nine rushes and to that we’ve got to improve in the run game.”
The Buccaneers are 0-3. Their coach, Todd Bowles, is on the hottest of hot seats.
Bowles isn’t a stupid coach, though. He’s seen the Packers’ season-long struggles in picking up blitzes and stunts.
He also knows the Packers will be counting on either struggling linemen or new linemen to pick up those blitzers. It’s likely to be the team’s fourth starting combination in as many games.
Because of porous pass protection, quarterback Jordan Love has taken a beating. Love has been sacked and hit a combined 38 times, according to Sumer Sports, which is the most in the NFL. And because he’s taken a beating, he’s been skittish in the pocket.
Bowles loves to blitz. Depending on whose data you look at, the Buccaneers are either second or third in blitz rate. So, even under ordinary circumstances, Bowles was going to be in attack mode against the Packers. In these extraordinary circumstances, Bowles is likely to crank up his level of aggressiveness.
“I’ve played them before,” one of those new linemen, Kevin Zeitler, said on Friday. “They’re extremely talented, great D-line depth. Obviously, head coach is a blitz monster.”
Last week, the Falcons tormented Love. Of his 55 dropbacks, he was under pressure on 25. The Falcons didn’t really blitz him, though. They got through with a variety of twists and stunts that the Packers failed to handle. He was blitzed 10 times, going 3-of-10 for 15 yards.
The not-so-simple starting point for the Packers will be figuring out who’s rushing and having blockers get in their way – a mission they failed at last week.
“Definitely. Playing quarterback, obviously, you always need time,” Love said. “The more time you have, the better you’re able to pick apart the defense and find those completions. That’s with anything, you always want time. Obviously, there’s times you might not have time; you’ve got to find those answers.
“That’s an area that we’ve got to improve on, is in pass pro just making sure we’re going to the right people and sustaining blocks for as long as we can, give me some time to pick the defense apart and obviously something that we need to improve on.”
Going to the “right people” would be a good start in giving Love a chance at making Bowles’ defense pay, because Love has done well against the blitz. According…

title: Top 10 Packers for Game at Buccaneers Include Newcomers, Homecoming
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers are a brand-new team. OK, not really, but they will probably look considerably different when they line up Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
This will be another tough road test in a first quarter of the season that has seen the Packers play on the road twice with mixed results.
Green Bay is 1-2, and the season is at risk of hitting a tailspin quickly. The month of October will see the Packers play five games against NFC foes, all of which are expected to compete for a spot in the postseason, including two divisional games against teams who will likely smell blood if the Packers continue to struggle.
Green Bay has not played well at Raymond James Stadium. They’re 3-8 there since the stadium opened in 2002. They’ll be faced with the usual weather hazards that can accompany a trip to Florida. The heat and humidity will be a factor.
Regardless of the weather, the Packers need a win, or the temperature at 1265 Lombardi Ave. will only get hotter.
Looking beyond the obvious for Jordan Love, here are the 10 most important players to making sure the Packers can cool things down before exiting Tampa Bay.
Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores blitzes the hell out of every quarterback he faces. The coach with the third-most pressures brought this season?
Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles.
Bowles used to be the king of sending pressure before Flores showed up to Minnesota and redefined what blitzing a quarterback means .
Who is going to be responsible for pointing out pressures? Jordan Love is part of that, but so is Sean Rhyan. That’s something that was added to his plate a season ago when he shifted from guard to center after Elgton Jenkins was lost for the season.
The Bucs bring pressure at a 46.2 percent clip. The Packers have shown no ability to slow down opposing pressure packages, so you can bet someone like Bowles is licking his chops to get after Love and continue to put him through misery. It’s up to Rhyan, and everyone who lines up next to him, to stop it.
“There was one pressure where they got through and hit Jordan pretty hard; that’s something we have to fix and make sure that doesn’t happen,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “That was a good pressure by them. But, other than that, it was just guys not sustaining their blocks and things like that. We need to do a better job.”
Who is going to step in for Jayden Reed? The backup to Reed all summer was Skyy Moore, and he’s been the next man up since Reed suffered a season-ending injury against the Jets with Savion Williams on injured reserve.
Moore’s expanded role on offense will not affect his presence in the return game, according to Matt LaFleur.
The Packers are going to need to find some secondary pass catchers somewhere. As good as Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have been to start the season, they cannot be relied on to carry an entire passing game. That’s a lot to ask for any duo of receivers.
Moore, with five catches to start the season, needs to be able to give them something in the middle of the field. He’s not going to be Reed, but if he can be a lighter version of him, that certainly would help.
“I’m ready, for sure,” Moore said. “I feel like this is what I prepared for. Just going out there and continue to do what I’ve been doing on special teams and add onto the offensive side of the ball.”
Perhaps it’s not a coincidence that Green Bay’s worst game of the year defensively came in a game that Edgerrin Cooper did not play well and exited early due to a concussion.
Cooper cleared the concussion protocol on Saturday and will be ready to roll on Sunday. With the unknown that rookie Jalon Daniels brings to the quarterback position, Cooper is likely the one who will be tasked with chasing down the rabbit-quick and oil-slick quarterback out of Kansas.
Look for Gannon to try and deploy Cooper in a variety of ways to keep Daniels in the pocket as best he can.
Who is going to catch passes for Tampa Bay? Mike Evans is in San Francisco. Jalen McMillan is hurt. Chris Godwin has not looked like himself with injuries piling up in his career.
That leaves star second-year receiver Emeka Egbuka. Egbuka was taken in the same class as Matthew Golden and was a star last year for the Bucs, falling just short of 1,000 yards as a rookie.
Cisse has had his ups and downs through three weeks of his rookie season, but will likely draw the assignment of Egbuka at some point, including key moments.
Usually, a backup quarterback is going to rely on his team’s best players. Daniels probably doesn’t have a lot of reps with Egbuka, but they’re likely going to draw some things up to get the ball in his hands and let him make plays after the catch.
If Cisse ends up with the primary assignment on Egbuka, he needs to limit him as much as possible. Making a rookie quarterback pat the ball is a win for the defense, and can lead to rookie mistakes.
When the Packers gave Devonte Wyatt a contract extension this offseason, the hope was that his best football was still in front of him now that he was fully removed from offseason surgery following last year’s season-ending ankle injury.
Through three weeks, that has not been the case. Wyatt has been largely invisible. He has two pressures, according to PFF, and it feels like there has been less than that.
Wyatt is supposed to be Green Bay’s best defensive lineman. With Warren Brinson sent to injured reserve and Anthony Campbell out again, a position that once had a lot of depth got really thin in a hurry.
“I think he’s in a good spot,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said about Wyatt on Tuesday. “He’s playing a lot of plays. I think he’s still catching his groove but he’s doing some good things, and I think he’ll keep impacting the game.”
They need him to catch his groove and start impacting the game as soon as Sunday.
The Packers signed three offensive linemen this week to fix their chronic problems at guard. With Aaron Banks out again, it feels like a good bet that one of those new guys, Laken Tomlinson, will start.
Tomlinson wasn’t with a team during training camp, but at least he opened the season on the Cowboys’ practice squad, so he’s likely in the best version of game shape of the newcomers.
Tomlinson gives the Packers some experience after Jager Burton gave up a whopping 10 pressures against the Falcons, according to PFF. Tomlinson may not be the player he once was, but he provides some experience and stability at a position group where the Packers desperately need some help.
“I feel like I can come in and provide some stability, some toughness, some leadership, as well,” Tomlinson said. “Obviously going into Year 12, I’ve played a lot of ball. I feel like I still got a lot left in the tank. I feel like I can bring a lot to the team.”
Tomlinson is right. He has played a lot of ball. If you remove Banks, both players who made starts at left guard for the Packers this season had a combined zero starts going into Week 1 and Week 3.
Tomlinson is a veteran. He’s seen just about everything.
“I think the reps definitely speeds up the process,” Tomlinson said. “The reps and the familiarity with the scheme. I feel like the process now is just being around the guys, working with the guys. That’s going to go a long way.”
Outside of his rookie season in 2023, Tucker Kraft may have just suffered his worst week with the Packers. Kraft struggled in the game on Thursday and has yet to hit his stride this season. He followed that up with some out-of-touch comments about the team being booed during the game.
What’s a good way to rebound? Be the productive player that Kraft has been since he hit his stride in the second half of 2023.
With Jayden Reed sidelined for the rest of the season, the Packers need someone in the passing game to join the party that has mostly consisted of just Matthew Golden and Christian Watson.

title: Winning Welcome: Three Reasons Why Packers Will Beat Buccaneers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have been a hot mess to begin the season. If it’s required a mop and bucket to handle their 1-2 start, it’s taken a hazmat suit for the Buccaneers to deal with their 0-3 open.
The Packers will win on Sunday – right? – and here’s why.
Sometimes, the simple analysis is the best analysis. The Packers’ quarterback is Jordan Love. The Buccaneers’ quarterback is Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie.
We probably could leave it at that and move onto the next item.
To say Love has had a rough start to the season would be an understatement. It’s been a rocky and painful start to the season.
It starts with being beaten like a pinata.
Only Carolina’s Bryce Young has faced more under-pressure dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. By percentage, only Young and Chicago’s Caleb Williams have faced a higher rate of under-pressure quarterbacks. No quarterback has taken more hits than Love, and too many of them have been of the wicked variety.
“That’s an area that we’ve got to improve on is in pass pro just making sure we’re going to the right people and sustaining blocks for as long as we can, give me some time to pick the defense apart,” Love said this week.
It was perhaps the most outspoken thing he’s said to the media in his career.
However, even while ranking last in the NFL in completion percentage, he’s fourth in yards and tied for 10th in touchdowns. He will be attacking against a Buccaneers defense that ranks 19th in opponent passer rating and will play without one of its top pass rushers, rookie first-round pick Rueben Bain.
“They're explosive,” Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said this week. “Tucker Kraft is playing very well. They've got the two young receivers outside in (Christian) Watson and (Matthew) Golden that [are] playing unbelievable – both very fast, as well. Then, (Love) puts the ball on a dime. He knows how to get rid of it, and he understands the offense very well.”
Daniels spent six seasons at Kansas. During his final season, he completed 62.1 percent of his passes with 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He added 550 rushing yards (sacks not counted against him) but fumbled 10 times.
This was his NFL.com scouting report from Lance Zierlein: “Daniels hasn’t shown the ability to consistently dissect defenses and win with accuracy from the pocket. He has a decent arm but lacks consistent mechanics, timing and three-level ball placement. The vast majority of his interceptions were due to a lack of coverage recognition. Daniels’ running ability helps, but he appears ill-prepared for an NFL passing game.”
Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon dove into Daniels’ tape from the preseason as well as in college to get a feel for this week’s matchup.
“We’ve got to turn over every stone,” he said.
Daniels is short (6-foot) and a good-but-not-great athlete with his 4.65 speed in the 40. When push comes to shove, he’d probably rather run than throw. The name of the game will be to confuse him and make him try to beat Green Bay’s secondary.
“It really don’t matter. If we can’t do our jobs, all 11, it don’t matter who’s at quarterback,” safety Xavier McKinney said. “Right now, everybody got to focus on doing their job, me, myself included, and we got to make plays when they’re there, but you got to trust the guy next to you to do his job. I think that’s all of what it really comes down to. So, we not worried about what they got going on in their side.”
Everybody knows the Packers’ biggest problem from the first three games.
Most importantly, general manager Brian Gutekunst figured out the Packers’ biggest problem from the first three games.
The offensive line was a disaster, starting with the play of the guards. Left guard Aaron Banks can’t get on the field or stay on the field. Jacob Monk, who was handed the job at right guard early in training camp, wasn’t up to the task. The next men up at left guard, Donovan Jennings and Jager Burton, were bad and worse.
So, Gutekunst pivoted by signing veterans Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler to the 53-man roster and Mekhi Becton to the practice squad.
Here’s Kevin Zeitler. He gets off the rock in a hurry. pic.twitter.com/erYBB8Fe9S
Between regular season and postseason, Tomlinson has played 10,867 snaps at left guard and Zeitler has played 14,403 snaps at right guard. That’s more than 25,000 snaps at their positions compared to the season-opening totals of six at left guard for Jennings, zero (obviously) at left guard for Burton and zero at right guard for Monk.
It remains to be seen how much they’ll play against the Buccaneers. Remember, neither player had a training camp and both players got three practices to learn the offense.
“An absolute whirlwind in every possible way,” Zeitler said on Friday .
Nonetheless, indications are Tomlinson would start at left guard and Zeitler seemed confident that he’d be ready to go at right guard.
Even 20 or 30 snaps from Tomlinson and Zeitler would be 20 or 30 snaps better than the alternative, especially against a defense that excels at stopping the run and loves to blitz.
Here's the Saturday roster news for the Packers, who now have a 52-man roster. Mekhi Becton was not elevated from the practice squad. https://t.co/w76QlBkjha
Green Bay’s run defense, which dominated the Jets’ excellent tandem of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen in Week 2, got dominated by the Falcons’ Bijan Robinson in Week 3.
The Packers will have to tackle another quality running back on Sunday with the Buccaneers’ Bucky Irving.
“He’s a top-tier running back,” coach Matt LaFleur said.
Irving as a rookie in 2024 rushed for 1,122 yards and topped 1,500 total yards. In three games this season, he’s rushed for 180 yards (4.5 average) and caught 13 passes. He’s a quality player – but he’s not Bijan Robinson, who rushed for 194 yards last week, frequently turning no-running-room plays into explosive gains.
“I don’t think it’s like, go back to the drawing board, I just think we’ve got to coach and play better. I know that’s cliché but it’s the truth,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said. “Obviously, give a lot of credit to Atlanta and what they did. I thought Bijan had a really good night. He made us miss some tackles.
“We had a lot of I would call them cup violations. We’ve got to do a better job caging the ball. When the ball circles you, it’s typically not good, and we had the ball circle us a couple times. But we’ve got the same challenge coming up between Bucky Irving and (Kenneth) Gainwell. If you give them your edge, they’re going to take your edge, so we’ve got to do a good job, set edges, building a wall and tackling.”
If the Packers play run defense like they did against the Jets, it will make it a one-dimensional game against a rookie quarterback. If that’s the case, the Packers should win – and perhaps comfortably.
